    6.1 What the unit and counit measure

    For a differential graded (dg) algebra BB, the ordinary derived category D(B)D(B) is obtained from complexes of BB-modules by inverting quasi-isomorphisms. We retain its enhancement, so derived mapping complexes and their composition remain available. There is no bound on cohomological degrees. As before, differentials raise degree by one and L[1]n=Ln+1L[1]^n=L^{n+1}.

    Let AA be another dg algebra and let WW be an AA-BB bimodule. Derived tensor and derived Hom give an adjunction

    Φ=W⊗B𝐋−:D(B)⇄D(A):Ψ=RHomA⁡(W,−).\Phi=W\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-:D(B) \rightleftarrows D(A): \Psi=\operatorname{RHom}_A(W,-).

    Its defining property is the natural equivalence

    RHomA⁡(ΦL,M)≃RHomB⁡(L,ΨM).\operatorname{RHom}_A(\Phi L,M) \simeq\operatorname{RHom}_B(L,\Psi M).

    The unit ηL:L→ΨΦL\eta_L:L\to\Psi\Phi L corresponds to the identity of ΦL\Phi L; the counit εM:ΦΨM→M\varepsilon_M:\Phi\Psi M\to M corresponds to the identity of ΨM\Psi M. In degree zero the counit is evaluation. Derived resolutions supply its meaning on complexes. These are adjunction maps, distinct from an algebra unit or a coalgebra counit.

    The two triangle identities are

    εΦL∘Φ(ηL)=1ΦL,Ψ(εM)∘ηΨM=1ΨM.\varepsilon_{\Phi L}\circ\Phi(\eta_L)=1_{\Phi L}, \qquad \Psi(\varepsilon_M)\circ\eta_{\Psi M}=1_{\Psi M}.

    They express compatibility of the two reconstructions. The functor Φ\Phi is fully faithful precisely when every ηL\eta_L is an equivalence. The functor Ψ\Psi is fully faithful precisely when every εM\varepsilon_M is an equivalence. An equivalence of the two whole categories requires both.

    Already extension of scalars requires the derived tensor. Put R=ℂ[x]R=\mathbb C[x] and K=R/(x)K=R/(x). The free resolution

    [R→xR]⟶K,\bigl[R\xrightarrow{x}R\bigr]\longrightarrow K,

    with the two free terms in degrees −1,0-1,0, gives

    K⊗R𝐋K≃[K→0K]≃K⊕︎K[1].K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K \simeq\bigl[K\xrightarrow{0}K\bigr] \simeq K\oplus K[1].

    Ordinary tensor retains only the degree-zero copy. The other copy records the relation x=0x=0. This is the simplest instance of the information carried by a bar resolution. Extension and restriction of scalars, with their derived adjunction, are described in the Stacks Project, Example 22.33.6.

    A right dg module PP is K-flat if P⊗BXP\otimes_B X is acyclic whenever the left dg module XX is acyclic. Such a module computes derived tensor on arbitrary coefficients. Dually, a complex JJ is K-injective if its Hom complex from every acyclic complex is acyclic. This condition concerns the whole complex; injectivity of each term alone does not suffice in the unbounded case. See the Stacks Project, §13.31.

    6.2 Affine currents and the algebra acting on their resolution

    Let 𝔤\mathfrak g be a nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra. Choose an invariant form κ\kappa, normalized so that long roots have squared length two, and write

    12tr⁡(ad⁡xad⁡y)=h∨κ(x,y).\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}x\,\operatorname{ad}y) =h^\vee\kappa(x,y).

    The integer h∨h^\vee is the dual Coxeter number. For a scalar parameter kk, set ℓ=(−k−h∨)κ\ell=(-k-h^\vee)\kappa. The affine mode algebra AℓA_\ell has relations

    [xtr,ytq]=[x,y]tr+q+rδr+q,0ℓ(x,y)1.[xt^r,yt^q]=[x,y]t^{r+q} +r\delta_{r+q,0}\ell(x,y)1.

    The scalar −k−h∨-k-h^\vee is its raw affine level: it is the coefficient of the central cocycle in this normalization. The mode algebra here has no degree derivation. Its internal energy grading assigns energy −r-r to xtrxt^r.

    Put

    𝔫=t𝔤[t],𝔩=𝔤[t−1],R=U(𝔤),H=U(𝔩).\mathfrak n=t\mathfrak g[t],\qquad \mathfrak l=\mathfrak g[t^{-1}],\qquad R=U(\mathfrak g),\qquad H=U(\mathfrak l).

    A module is smooth if each vector is annihilated by tN𝔤[t]t^N\mathfrak g[t] for some NN, which may depend on the vector. Consider the induced smooth module

    W=Aℓ⊗U(𝔫)ℂ.W=A_\ell\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n)}\mathbb C.

    The Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt theorem identifies its underlying vector space with HH. Its energy-zero part is the regular RR-module. This distinguishes WW from the scalar-top vacuum

    V=Aℓ⊗U(𝔤[t])ℂ,V=A_\ell\otimes_{U(\mathfrak g[t])}\mathbb C,

    whose energy-zero part is ℂ\mathbb C.

    The polynomial dg algebra B=Yk(𝔤)B=Y_k(\mathfrak g) has even generators bmab_m^a and odd generators ca,mc_{a,m}, for m≥0m\ge0. Fix a basis tat_a, write [ta,tb]=fabctc[t_a,t_b]=f_{ab}{}^ct_c, and sum repeated Lie-algebra indices. Its relations and differential are

    [bma,bnb]=fabcbm+nc,[bma,cb,n]=−facbcc,m+n,ca,mcb,n=−cb,nca,m,dca,m=12fbca∑r+p=m−1cb,rcc,p,dbma=mkκabcb,m−1+12fabc∑r+p=m−1(cb,rbpc+bpccb,r).\begin{aligned} [b_m^a,b_n^b]&=f_{ab}{}^cb_{m+n}^c,\\ [b_m^a,c_{b,n}]&=-f_{ac}{}^bc_{c,m+n}, &c_{a,m}c_{b,n}&=-c_{b,n}c_{a,m},\\ dc_{a,m}&=\tfrac12f_{bc}{}^a \sum_{r+p=m-1}c_{b,r}c_{c,p},\\ db_m^a&=mk\kappa_{ab}c_{b,m-1} +\tfrac12f_{ab}{}^c \sum_{r+p=m-1}(c_{b,r}b_p^c+b_p^cc_{b,r}). \end{aligned}

    Negative indices contribute nothing. The cohomological degrees of b,cb,c are 0,10,1; their internal weights are m,m+1m,m+1. The differential preserves weight. The odd generators are often called ghosts; here that word means these specified degree-one algebra generators.

    Write BwB_w for the entire weight-ww complex. Then

    B=⨁w≥0Bw,B0=R,I=⨁w>0Bw.B=\bigoplus_{w\ge0}B_w,\qquad B_0=R,\qquad I=\bigoplus_{w>0}B_w.

    There are two useful quotients:

    B→qH→e0R,q(ca,m)=0,q(bma)=tat−m.B\xrightarrow{q}H\xrightarrow{e_0}R,\qquad q(c_{a,m})=0,\quad q(b_m^a)=t_at^{-m}.

    The map e0e_0 kills the strictly negative modes. Thus p=e0qp=e_0q is weight-zero projection and I=ker⁡pI=\ker p. These quotients forget different information. An HH-module inflated along qq has zero ghost action but may have nonzero negative-current action. Inflation from RR kills both.

    The affine Chevalley resolution of WW has

    P−p=Aℓ⊗Λp𝔫.P^{-p}=A_\ell\otimes\Lambda^p\mathfrak n.

    Its differential combines current multiplication with the Lie bracket. For x∈𝔩x\in\mathfrak l, let axa_x be the exterior derivation induced by y↦pr𝔫⁡[x,y]y\mapsto\operatorname{pr}_{\mathfrak n}[x,y]. The generators act on this resolution through

    ρ(bma)=Rtat−m−atat−m,ρ(ca,m)=ιa,m+1,\rho(b_m^a)=R_{t_at^{-m}}-a_{t_at^{-m}}, \qquad \rho(c_{a,m})=\iota_{a,m+1},

    where RxR_x is right multiplication on the affine factor and ιa,m+1\iota_{a,m+1} is contraction with the indicated positive mode. This specified generator action is called the native action. The correction axa_x is essential: its commutator supplies the half-Killing-form shift in ℓ\ell. With the graded opposite composition, these operators give the algebraic derived endomorphism comparison. This construction is developed in A derived endomorphism model for the line algebra, the affine-resolution and generator-lift sections.

    We must specify an additional smooth realization before using ordinary smooth derived Hom. Assume that the operators above are realized by a coherent right-BB object 𝒲\mathcal W in 𝒮ℓ=D(Sm⁡(Aℓ))\mathscr S_\ell=D(\operatorname{Sm}(A_\ell)), with underlying object WW. Assume the prescribed homogeneous endomorphism comparison and the compatible smooth Taylor resolutions

    PN=(Aℓ/Aℓ𝔫N)⊗Λ∙(𝔫/𝔫N),𝔫N=tN𝔤[t],P_N=(A_\ell/A_\ell\mathfrak n_N) \otimes\Lambda^\bullet(\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n_N), \qquad \mathfrak n_N=t^N\mathfrak g[t],

    including their action comparisons on a common sufficiently large cutoff for each finite operator diagram. “Coherent” here includes all the higher compatibility homotopies for the right action. Finally assume the resulting enhanced adjunction

    Φ=𝒲⊗B𝐋−:D(B)⇄𝒮ℓ:Ψ=RHomSm⁡(Aℓ)⁡(𝒲,−).\Phi=\mathcal W\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-: D(B)\rightleftarrows\mathscr S_\ell: \Psi=\operatorname{RHom}_{\operatorname{Sm}(A_\ell)}(\mathcal W,-).
    (6.1)

    These are the smooth realization hypotheses used below. They identify a particular action and adjunction; they do not assert the desired unit theorem. They also keep smooth derived Hom distinct from derived Hom in all algebraic AℓA_\ell-modules.

    There is a parallel internally graded version. Modules are algebraic direct sums of their energy components, with arbitrary support. Set L⟨r⟩w=Lw−rL\langle r\rangle_w=L_{w-r}. Mapping complexes are formed at a specified homogeneous shift; their outer sum is algebraic. Neither convention introduces an energy completion.

    6.3 Cofree coefficients give the first unit theorem

    The restricted positive-current dual

    C𝔤=⨁E≥0U(𝔫)E∨C_{\mathfrak g}=\bigoplus_{E\ge0}U(\mathfrak n)_E^\vee

    uses the positive current degree deg⁡(xtr)=r\deg(xt^r)=r. Each summand is finite dimensional, and every element of C𝔤C_{\mathfrak g} has finite support in this degree. Put

    (Lxϕ)(u)=ϕ(xu),(Dxϕ)(u)=ϕ(ux).(L_x\phi)(u)=\phi(xu),\qquad (D_x\phi)(u)=\phi(ux).

    Both actions lower the support bound of a functional. For a homogeneous positive-current basis xi=tatrx_i=t_at^r, write ci=ca,r−1c_i=c_{a,r-1}. The complex

    𝒬=C𝔤⊗B,d𝒬(ϕ⊗b)=ϕ⊗db+∑iLxiϕ⊗cib\mathcal Q=C_{\mathfrak g}\otimes B,\qquad d_{\mathcal Q}(\phi\otimes b) =\phi\otimes db+\sum_iL_{x_i}\phi\otimes c_i b
    (6.2)

    has a pointwise finite differential. Its support filtration makes it semifree as a right BB-module: the differential of a new free generator uses generators of smaller support degree.

    The full affine action is restricted coinduction. Using the even HH-action on the underlying graded algebra BB, identify 𝒬\mathcal Q with

    {f∈HomH⁡(Aℓ,B):f|U(𝔫)≥d=0 for some d},(af)(b)=f(ba).\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_H(A_\ell,B): f|_{U(\mathfrak n)_{\ge d}}=0\text{ for some }d\}, \qquad (af)(b)=f(ba).

    The Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt decomposition gives the preceding tensor description. The twist in (6.2) makes its differential affine-linear at precisely the level ℓ=(−k−h∨)κ\ell=(-k-h^\vee)\kappa.

    Under the smooth realization hypotheses, 𝒬\mathcal Q is equivalent to the whole coherent right-BB object 𝒲\mathcal W, with its affine action retained. Consequently it computes ΦL\Phi L for every ordinary unbounded LL. This is the cofree-model theorem in The cofree native model and inflated-base unit for every simple Lie algebra. The comparison preserves the specified action on PP.

    If TT is an arbitrary unbounded HH-complex inflated to BB, every ghost acts by zero. Formula (6.2) becomes

    ΦT≃(C𝔤⊗T,1⊗dT).\Phi T\simeq(C_{\mathfrak g}\otimes T,1\otimes d_T).

    Its positive-current action is DD on the first factor. The restricted dual with arbitrary vector-space coefficients is injective in the smooth positive-current category. More is needed for an unbounded TT: split its underlying complex over ℂ\mathbb C into its cohomology and a contractible complex. Tensoring this splitting with C𝔤C_{\mathfrak g} is positive-current-linear. It exhibits the restriction as homotopy equivalent to a product of injectives placed in single degrees, hence as K-injective. At each degree only one of those factors contributes; no completion of C𝔤C_{\mathfrak g} is involved.

    The positive-current invariants are exactly δ1⊗T\delta_1\otimes T, where δ1\delta_1 extracts the scalar coefficient of U(𝔫)U(\mathfrak n). Evaluation on this vector identifies the original signed tensor–Hom unit with the identity of TT.

    Conditional unit theorem for inflated coefficients. For every simple 𝔤\mathfrak g and every k∈ℂk\in\mathbb C, under the smooth realization hypotheses of (6.1), the actual unit

    T→ηTΨΦTT\xrightarrow{\eta_T}\Psi\Phi T

    is an equivalence for every ordinary unbounded HH-complex inflated along qq, and therefore for every inflated RR-complex. This holds with arbitrary algebraic internal support or without an internal grading.

    The theorem includes critical affine level. It also includes raw 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 level −3-3. Its proof uses the zero ghost action on these coefficients; the cofree realization formula alone does not establish the unit for a general BB-module.

    6.4 Finite descent from a quotient

    To reach modules with nonzero ghost action, consider first a general split dg algebra extension

    R⟶B→pR,p|R=1,I=ker⁡p.R\longrightarrow B\xrightarrow{p}R,\qquad p|_R=1, \qquad I=\ker p.

    Assume RR is an ordinary algebra, BB is K-flat on both RR-sides, and for a finite integer NN,

    I⊗R𝐋N≃0as a complex of R-bimodules.I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N}\simeq0 \quad\text{as a complex of \(R\)-bimodules}.
    (6.3)

    The two multiplication actions are part of this assertion; RR need not be central.

    Let F=R⊗B𝐋−F=R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-, and let UU be restriction of scalars along pp, also called inflation. A relative bar resolution converts (6.3) into vanishing of the NN-fold derived tensor of II over BB. For every LL, put

    Tj(L)=I⊗B𝐋j⊗B𝐋L,T0(L)=L.T_j(L)=I^{\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}j} \otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L,\qquad T_0(L)=L.

    There is a functorial tower

    0≃TN(L)⟶TN−1(L)⟶⋯⟶T0(L)=L0\simeq T_N(L)\longrightarrow T_{N-1}(L) \longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow T_0(L)=L
    (6.4)

    whose triangles are

    Tj+1(L)⟶Tj(L)→uTj(L)UF(Tj(L))⟶Tj+1(L)[1].T_{j+1}(L)\longrightarrow T_j(L) \xrightarrow{u_{T_j(L)}}UF(T_j(L)) \longrightarrow T_{j+1}(L)[1].
    (6.5)

    Here uu is the scalar-extension unit, distinct from η\eta in (6.1). Every cofiber is inflated from an unrestricted RR-complex with its actual outer RR-action.

    The bar argument explains the change of base from RR to BB. Resolve an II-factor by terms

    (I⊗RI⊗Rq⊗RB)[q],q≥0.\bigl(I\otimes_R I^{\otimes_R q}\otimes_R B\bigr)[q], \qquad q\ge0.

    In an NN-fold derived tensor over BB, each resulting bar term contains at least NN copies of II tensored over RR. Such a term is acyclic by (6.3) and the two-sided K-flatness. Finite bar-length filtrations and their exact algebraic union prove the asserted vanishing without a cohomological bound.

    For an exact enhanced adjunction Φ⊣Ψ\Phi\dashv\Psi, the class of objects on which its unit is invertible is closed under finite triangles and retracts. Thus (6.4) proves:

    Finite descent theorem. Under the split-extension, K-flatness and tensor-vanishing hypotheses above, the actual unit is invertible on every L∈D(B)L\in D(B) if it is invertible on every unrestricted inflated RR-complex.

    The proof propagates the same natural transformation through (6.5). It never assumes that Ψ\Psi preserves an infinite coproduct. The construction and its map identifications are given in A finite filtration from derived tensor nilpotence, Theorems A–B.

    Ordinary ideal multiplication cannot replace (6.3). For B=ℂ[ϵ]/(ϵ2)B=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2), R=ℂR=\mathbb C and I=(ϵ)I=(\epsilon), one has I2=0I^2=0, but

    I⊗ℂN≅ℂ(N≥1).I^{\otimes_{\mathbb C}N}\cong\mathbb C \qquad(N\ge1).

    The multiplication of two ideal elements vanishes; the tensor of those elements remains nonzero.

    There is a second, weaker sufficient criterion. For a dg algebra map B→HB\to H, form its fibre J→B→HJ\to B\to H in the derived category of genuine BB-bimodules. It suffices that one tensor power of the fibre-inclusion map

    μN:J⊗B𝐋N⟶B\mu_N:J^{\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N}\longrightarrow B
    (6.6)

    be zero as a bimodule morphism, together with invertibility of the unit on all inflated unbounded HH-complexes. The tensor object in (6.6) need not vanish. A fixed bimodule nullhomotopy makes BB a retract of cofib⁡(μN)\operatorname{cofib}(\mu_N); the latter is a finite extension of bimodules whose left action factors through HH. Tensoring this one diagram with LL gives a coefficient-functorial retract and proves the unit theorem. See Finite bimodule descent for the actual adjunction unit, Theorem 1.1.

    6.5 Four factors suffice for nonrational 𝔰𝔩3\mathfrak{sl}_3

    Now take

    𝔤=𝔰𝔩3(ℂ),κ(x,y)=Tr⁡(xy),s∈ℂ∖ℚ,B=Y−s.\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3(\mathbb C),\qquad \kappa(x,y)=\operatorname{Tr}(xy),\qquad s\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q,\qquad B=Y_{-s}.

    The raw affine level is s−3s-3. The complement of ℚ\mathbb Q here includes nonreal complex parameters. With R=U(𝔰𝔩3)R=U(\mathfrak{sl}_3) and I=⨁w>0BwI=\bigoplus_{w>0}B_w, the algebraic theorem is

    I⊗R𝐋4≃0,I⊗R𝐋3≄0.I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}4}\simeq0, \qquad I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}3}\not\simeq0.
    (6.7)

    Four is the smallest vanishing exponent. Both statements use the original two RR-actions and hold with the grading retained or forgotten.

    The finite exponent comes from a bound on possible representation-theoretic transitions. Choose the diagonal Cartan subalgebra 𝔥⊂𝔰𝔩3\mathfrak h\subset\mathfrak{sl}_3 and the positive roots determined by upper-triangular matrices, and put ρ=12∑α>0α\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha>0}\alpha, the finite Weyl vector. For an affine highest weight ξ\xi, let μ=ξ|𝔥+ρ\mu=\xi|_{\mathfrak h}+\rho. A real affine root α+nδ\alpha+n\delta is integral for this weight precisely when

    (μ,α)+ns∈ℤ.(\mu,\alpha)+ns\in\mathbb Z.

    For each finite root α\alpha, there is at most one such nn. Otherwise a nonzero integer multiple of ss would be an integer. The integral reflection group therefore has type 11, A1A_1, or A2A_2, with longest Coxeter length at most three.

    This observation becomes a tensor theorem through a specific comparison. A horizontal Verma module is the highest-weight U(𝔤)U(\mathfrak g)-module induced from a one-dimensional representation of a Borel subalgebra. For a horizontal module NN in the bounded category-O range, the actual complex

    Bm⊗R𝐋NB_m\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N

    computes positive-current derived invariants in energy a+ma+m of the affine module induced from NN placed at energy aa. Category O here consists of weight modules with locally finite positive-root action and the stated highest-weight finiteness conditions.

    For m>0m>0, every surviving component makes a strict transition in a finite Bruhat order, the order on reflection words determined by inclusion of reduced subwords. The relevant states are parabolic double cosets: the left parabolic records integral zero-mode roots, and the right parabolic records the stabilizer of the affine highest weight. The length of the largest element in a state lies between zero and three and strictly increases along a surviving transition. Four successive positive weights cannot survive.

    Each fixed tensor word is a bounded complex of finitely generated bimodules with locally finite diagonal adjoint action xv−vxxv-vx. These are the Harish–Chandra bimodule conditions used here. A detection theorem for these complexes promotes vanishing on all horizontal Verma tests to vanishing of the actual bimodule tensor words. Summing those words algebraically proves the first assertion of (6.7). The nonzero third power has the weight word B1⊗R𝐋B2⊗R𝐋B1B_1\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_2\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_1. These are the mechanisms in The fourth derived tensor power of the native sl3 positive ideal, §§1–6, together with the third-power theorem. The finite-block input uses Fiebig, The combinatorics of category O for symmetrizable Kac–Moody algebras, Theorem 2.2 and §§2.3–2.4 (arXiv:math/0305378v2).

    Conditional full-unit theorem. Let B=Y−s(𝔰𝔩3)B=Y_{-s}(\mathfrak{sl}_3), s∈ℂ∖ℚs\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q, and let the affine algebra have raw level s−3s-3 with form Tr⁡(xy)\operatorname{Tr}(xy). Assume the smooth realization data of (6.1), including the specified right action, homogeneous endomorphism comparison, Taylor-resolution coherences and actual enhanced tensor–Hom adjunction. Then

    ηL:L→∼ΨΦL\eta_L:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi\Phi L

    for every ordinary cohomologically unbounded BB-complex, either ungraded or algebraically internally graded with arbitrary support.

    Its proof has four concrete steps. First, the weight-zero projection is a split dg augmentation. Each BwB_w is a bounded complex whose terms are free on each RR-side, so the required K-flatness holds on both sides. Second, (6.7) supplies the fourth-power vanishing. Third, B→H→RB\to H\to R and the inflated-coefficient theorem identify the actual unit on every inflated RR-complex. Fourth, the tower (6.4) with N=4N=4 propagates that unit to every LL. No assertion about Ψ\Psi on infinite sums enters this argument.

    The same tower gives an algebraic consequence independent of the smooth realization: every LL has at most four inflated RR-complex factors, and R⊗B𝐋−R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}- is conservative. Indeed, if F(L)=0F(L)=0, the first triangle makes I⊗B𝐋L→LI\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L\to L an equivalence. Iterating four times identifies LL with zero. The theorem and these consequences are established in The full ordinary native unit for sl3 at nonrational parameter, §§1–3. For Yk(𝔰𝔩2)Y_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2), k∈ℂ∖ℚk\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q, the corresponding conditional full-unit theorem uses a square-zero derived ideal and a two-factor reduction.

    6.6 The image and its original counit

    Write Loc⁡(W)\operatorname{Loc}(W) for the smallest full stable subcategory containing WW and closed under arbitrary coproducts and retracts. In the internally graded case use all energy shifts:

    𝒞={Loc𝒮ℓ⁡(W),ungraded,Loc𝒮ℓ⁡{W⟨r⟩:r∈ℤ},graded.\mathscr C= \begin{cases} \operatorname{Loc}_{\mathscr S_\ell}(W),&\text{ungraded},\\ \operatorname{Loc}_{\mathscr S_\ell} \{W\langle r\rangle:r\in\mathbb Z\},&\text{graded}. \end{cases}

    Under the preceding full-unit theorem,

    D(B)≃𝒞.D(B)\simeq\mathscr C.
    (6.8)

    The source is generated by BB, or by all its internal shifts, using semifree resolutions. The left adjoint preserves coproducts and sends these generators to WW and its shifts. Full faithfulness also lifts cones and retracts between image objects. These facts identify the image exactly with 𝒞\mathscr C.

    The original counit, not an independently chosen evaluation, is the coreflection into this image:

    ΦΨM→εMM.\Phi\Psi M\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_M}M.

    This means that for every C∈𝒞C\in\mathscr C, it induces an equivalence on derived maps from CC. To prove it, the second triangle identity and the full-unit theorem give

    Ψ(εM)=ηΨM−1.\Psi(\varepsilon_M)=\eta_{\Psi M}^{-1}.

    The cone of εM\varepsilon_M is therefore killed by Ψ\Psi, hence is right-orthogonal to 𝒞\mathscr C. In particular, (6.8) identifies a specified part of the smooth category; it does not assert that every smooth object lies there.

    An object is compact in a category if maps from it commute with arbitrary coproducts. The free module BB is compact in D(B)D(B), so WW is compact inside 𝒞\mathscr C, with all shifts included when graded. This is a relative compactness assertion. It makes no claim about mapping from WW into arbitrary families outside 𝒞\mathscr C. The image, compactness and original-counit statements are proved in the same manuscript, §§4–6.

    6.7 Infinite extensions at other levels

    Finite descent explains why the nonrational theorem reaches unbounded coefficients. Without it, invertibility on every finite stage need not survive an infinite construction.

    At critical raw level −h∨-h^\vee, take B=Y0B=Y_0 and

    E=B⊗R𝐋ℂ,ΦE≃V.E=B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\mathbb C,\qquad \Phi E\simeq V.

    Assume the smooth realization and its actual lower-energy unit theorem. Critical vacuum cohomology supplies extension classes

    V⟶V[1]⟨−(n+2)⟩,n≥0,V\longrightarrow V[1]\langle-(n+2)\rangle,\qquad n\ge0,

    whose finite consecutive products are all nonzero. Their construction uses the quadratic central field and its successive derivatives. The level-deformation classes correspond to differentials of independent polynomial coordinates under the Frenkel–Teleman theorem: Self-extensions of Verma modules and differential forms on opers, Theorem 4.4 (arXiv:math/0401428).

    Lift these classes through the unit on the individually lower-weight-bounded objects and form

    L=hocolimr≥0⁡E[r]⟨−r(r+3)2⟩.L=\operatorname*{hocolim}_{r\ge0} E[r]\left\langle-\frac{r(r+3)}2\right\rangle.
    (6.9)

    A sequential homotopy colimit is the cone of 1−shift1-\mathrm{shift} on the direct sum of its terms. Compactness of EE detects a nonzero map E→LE\to L: its successive representatives are precisely the nonzero extension products. Thus L≠0L\ne0.

    After realization, the terms are shifted copies of the module VV, concentrated in different cohomological degrees. Every transition induces zero on cohomology, so 1−shift1-\mathrm{shift} induces the identity on the cohomology of the direct sum. Its cone is zero. Consequently

    L≠0,ΦL=0,ηL:L⟶0.L\ne0,\qquad \Phi L=0,\qquad \eta_L:L\longrightarrow0.

    The lower weight bounds in (6.9) tend to minus infinity. Each finite stage keeps its valid unit. This is the theorem of A critical-level kernel of the ordinary first-kind realization, §§1–4, conditional on its specified smooth realization and lower-energy comparison.

    Related extension telescopes give kernels at raw 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 levels −4,−5,…-4,-5,\ldots, and at raw level −2h∨-2h^\vee for every simple type, under the corresponding realization and lower-energy hypotheses. They also show that WW can fail to be compact even in its own generated category. The precise sources are Actual-unit kernels at negative integral shifted sl2 levels and A noncritical ordinary-unit kernel for every simple Lie algebra.

    These ordinary-derived statements coexist with an all-type, all-level induction equivalence using different weak equivalences. For dg YkY_k-modules that are termwise algebraically smooth for the even modes, twisted induction at raw level k−h∨k-h^\vee has an explicit restricted twisted-coinduction inverse after inverting exactly the maps that induction sends to affine quasi-isomorphisms. That class is a proper subclass of the ordinary quasi-isomorphisms. This source localization therefore retains information that localization at all ordinary quasi-isomorphisms discards. This is the equivalence in Corrected induction: the inverse, the adjunction and the equivalence, Theorem 8.1. Its functor, level convention and source localization are part of the statement.

    6.8 Raw level minus three distinguishes the two quotients

    For 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 at raw level −3-3, the line algebra is B=Y1B=Y_1. Let

    Vj=V(−2j−1),Fj=(B⊗RVj)⟨−j2⟩,V_j=V(-2j-1),\qquad F_j=(B\otimes_RV_j)\langle-j^2\rangle,

    where V(λ)V(\lambda) is the horizontal Verma module of highest weight λ\lambda. There are actual degree-zero maps βj:Fj−1→Fj\beta_j:F_{j-1}\to F_j represented by positive-weight cycles. Their affine realizations send highest vectors to

    vj−1⟼f02j−2e−12j−1vj.v_{j-1}\longmapsto f_0^{\,2j-2}e_{-1}^{\,2j-1}v_j.
    (6.10)

    Here f0f_0 is the horizontal lowering current and e−1e_{-1} the mode-−1-1 raising current. These are injective maps of affine Verma modules.

    For L=hocolimj⁡(Fj,βj)L=\operatorname{hocolim}_j(F_j,\beta_j), the two quotients have different effects:

    R⊗B𝐋L=0,H⊗B𝐋L≠0,ΦL≠0.R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L=0,\qquad H\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L\ne0,\qquad \Phi L\ne0.
    (6.11)

    Projection to RR kills every positive-weight transition, and a telescope with zero transitions is zero. Projection to HH retains the ghost-free word (6.10). The resulting system consists of injective Verma maps and has a nonzero filtered colimit; the affine realization has the same property.

    Moreover, for I=ker⁡(B→R)I=\ker(B\to R), every finite map

    I⊗B𝐋N⟶BI^{\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N}\longrightarrow B

    induced by the ideal inclusion is nonzero. Thus both the tensor-object and fibre-map descent routes through B→RB\to R fail at this parameter. The proof is A nonzero native telescope killed by the zero-weight augmentation, §§2–4.

    The ghost quotient B→HB\to H has a different fibre, and (6.11) gives no obstruction to its finite fibre-map criterion. The unit is already invertible on every inflated HH-complex. It is also invertible on every B⊗R𝐋TB\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}T for an arbitrary unbounded horizontal RR-complex TT, by A finite cofree resolution for arbitrary horizontal coefficients at raw level minus three. Whether the unit is invertible on every BB-complex at this level remains open. The object in (6.11) is not an affine-realization kernel.

    6.9 Cellularity and derived torsion

    There is another plausible description of the image in (6.8), expressed directly in positive-current modules. To keep its ideal distinct from I⊂YkI\subset Y_k, put

    U+=U(t𝔤[t]),𝔞=ker⁡(U+→ℂ).U_+=U(t\mathfrak g[t]),\qquad \mathfrak a=\ker(U_+\to\mathbb C).

    A smooth module is jointly augmentation-torsion if every vector vv is killed by one whole power 𝔞r\mathfrak a^r. The exponent may depend on vv, but it must work for every element of that ideal power. Let 𝒯⊂Sm⁡(Aℓ)\mathcal T\subset\operatorname{Sm}(A_\ell) be this torsion category and set

    D𝔞={M∈𝒮ℓ:Hq(M)∈𝒯 for every q}.D_{\mathfrak a}= \{M\in\mathscr S_\ell:H^q(M)\in\mathcal T \text{ for every }q\}.

    The cellular category 𝒞\mathscr C generated by WW and its required shifts lies in D𝔞D_{\mathfrak a}.

    Finite augmentation quotients explain a substantial converse. Since 𝔤\mathfrak g is simple, U+U_+ is generated in positive current degree one, and

    𝔞r=⨁d≥r(U+)d.\mathfrak a^r=\bigoplus_{d\ge r}(U_+)_d.

    The quotient U+/𝔞rU_+/\mathfrak a^r is finite dimensional. The induced module

    Er=Aℓ⊗U+(U+/𝔞r)E_r=A_\ell\otimes_{U_+}(U_+/\mathfrak a^r)

    has a finite filtration with factors

    W⟨−j⟩⊗ℂ(U+)j,0≤j<r,W\langle-j\rangle\otimes_{\mathbb C}(U_+)_j, \qquad 0\le j<r,

    where the last factor is a multiplicity space. Resolutions by such modules show that every complex whose terms are torsion is cellular. Every object with bounded-below torsion cohomology is also cellular. These statements, and the cellular coreflector on the whole unbounded smooth category, are proved in Augmentation torsion and unbounded affine cellularization.

    The torsion inclusion has its own derived adjunction,

    i:D(𝒯)⇄D(Sm⁡(Aℓ)):RΓ𝔞.i:D(\mathcal T)\rightleftarrows D(\operatorname{Sm}(A_\ell)):R\Gamma_{\mathfrak a}.
    (6.12)

    It differs from both (6.1) and the inclusion of 𝒞\mathscr C. In particular, the exact inclusion of abelian categories need not induce a fully faithful functor on their unbounded derived categories.

    This failure occurs already for positive-current 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2, before adjoining negative affine modes. Let 𝒮+=Sm⁡(t𝔰𝔩2[t])\mathcal S_+=\operatorname{Sm}(t\mathfrak{sl}_2[t]), let 𝒯+\mathcal T_+ be its joint-torsion subcategory, and put

    en=n(n+1)2,X=⨁n≥1ℂ[n]⟨−en⟩.e_n=\frac{n(n+1)}2,\qquad X=\bigoplus_{n\ge1}\mathbb C[n]\langle-e_n\rangle.

    For the actual derived torsion adjunction one has

    H0RΓ𝔞(iX)0≅∏n≥1Kn⨁n≥1Kn≠0,dim⁡Kn=2n+1.H^0R\Gamma_{\mathfrak a}(iX)_0 \cong \frac{\prod_{n\ge1}K_n}{\bigoplus_{n\ge1}K_n}\ne0, \qquad \dim K_n=2n+1.
    (6.13)

    But H0X=0H^0X=0. Hence the unit of this torsion adjunction is not invertible. Its counit on the cellular object iXiX also fails to be an equivalence, so it cannot be the cellular coreflection there. Without an energy grading the corresponding quotient still injects into degree-zero cohomology. An explicit positive-current splitting transfers the failure to affine raw level zero; no transfer to arbitrary affine level is asserted. See An unbounded joint-torsion unit failure for positive-current sl2.

    Finite quotients nevertheless admit a precise local-duality theorem. For an integer N≥1N\ge1, put

    𝔫=t𝔰𝔩2[t],𝔤N=𝔫/tN𝔰𝔩2[t],RN=U(𝔤N),dN=3(N−1).\mathfrak n=t\mathfrak{sl}_2[t],\quad \mathfrak g_N=\mathfrak n/t^N\mathfrak{sl}_2[t],\quad R_N=U(\mathfrak g_N),\quad d_N=3(N-1).

    Let JNJ_N be the augmentation ideal of RNR_N and ENcof=lim→r⁡(RN/JNr)∨E_N^{\mathrm{cof}}=\varinjlim_r(R_N/J_N^r)^\vee, with action (bϕ)(a)=ϕ(ab)(b\phi)(a)=\phi(ab). In the actual positive-current smooth category,

    RΓ𝔞(RN)≃ENcof⊗(det⁡𝔤N)∨[−dN].R\Gamma_{\mathfrak a}(R_N) \simeq E_N^{\mathrm{cof}}\otimes (\det\mathfrak g_N)^\vee[-d_N].
    (6.14)

    The comparison identifies the actual torsion counit. In the graded convention the determinant-dual line has energy 3N(N−1)/23N(N-1)/2. The proof first uses finite-dimensional Lie-algebra duality, then compares the inflated counit cone through finite Chevalley complexes with bounded coefficient terms. It proves (6.14) for these objects, not a formula on arbitrary unbounded coefficients. See Actual torsion of the smooth regular quotients and its finite-quotient local-duality argument.

    The full unbounded equality 𝒞=D𝔞\mathscr C=D_{\mathfrak a} remains a separate question. Non-full-faithfulness of (6.12) does not decide that equality of object classes. Nor does termwise vanishing of a torsion functor prove vanishing of its derived value: a concrete quotient complex in the graded positive-current category has zero torsion in every term but is cellular and has nonzero actual derived torsion. K-injective replacement changes the calculation. This example is computed in The graded quotient does not give an outside or kernel object.

    A common current tail gives actual completeness

    Smooth-vector completeness is a different comparison from affine induction and from derived augmentation torsion. Put

    𝔫=t𝔰𝔩2[t],𝔫L=tL𝔰𝔩2[t],F:D(𝒮)⟶D(𝔐),G=Rsm⁡,\mathfrak n=t\mathfrak{sl}_2[t],\qquad \mathfrak n_L=t^L\mathfrak{sl}_2[t],\qquad F:D(\mathcal S)\longrightarrow D(\mathfrak M), \quad G=R\operatorname{sm},

    where 𝒮\mathcal S is the smooth positive-current module category and 𝔐\mathfrak M is the category of all positive-current modules. Use algebraic integer-energy gradings, with currents lowering energy and maps preserving it. Products are taken energy by energy before the outer algebraic direct sum.

    Suppose one tail annihilates all sufficiently low cohomology: there are L≥1L\ge1 and an integer bb such that

    𝔫LHq(X)=0(q≤b).\mathfrak n_LH^q(X)=0\qquad(q\le b).

    Then the actual unit is an equivalence,

    X→∼GF(X)≃holimn⁡τ≥−nX,X\xrightarrow{\sim}GF(X) \simeq\operatorname{holim}_n\tau^{\ge-n}X,

    with no bound on higher cohomology, multiplicities or energy support. For every smooth derived source YY, the original map

    HomD(𝒮)⁡(Y,X)⟶HomD(𝔐)⁡(FY,FX)\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal S)}(Y,X) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathfrak M)}(FY,FX)

    is an isomorphism, including all shifts. Common-tail completeness.

    The proof first restricts to a tail on which the cohomology layers are genuinely trivial. A sufficiently deeper restriction splits the Postnikov extensions coherently enough to identify the original completion map. If the same annihilating tail works in every degree, the whole restricted complex becomes noncanonically formal; M=4L−2M=4L-2 is a sufficient deeper-tail index. With the hypothesis only for q≤bq\le b, this formality statement applies to the lower truncation. No formality over the original positive-current algebra is asserted.

    Completeness does not settle generation by the shifted trivial modules. Writing

    ℒ=Loc⁡{ℂ⟨e⟩:e∈ℤ},\mathcal L=\operatorname{Loc}\{\mathbb C\langle e\rangle:e\in\mathbb Z\},

    the equality of ℒ\mathcal L with the full subcategory of joint augmentation-torsion cohomology remains open. A potential nonzero torsion-cohomology object in ℒ⟂\mathcal L^\perp may be complete and may have a common annihilating tail; its current action must be nontrivial in arbitrarily low cohomological degrees. The smooth derived category is itself not left-complete. The common-tail theorem locates a large complete class within it, rather than identifying completeness with cellularity. The separate generation question.

    We therefore have a representation-theoretic equivalence onto a specified generated category in the nonrational 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 and 𝔰𝔩3\mathfrak{sl}_3 cases, explicit kernels at other levels, and a distinct unbounded torsion problem. A comparison with a physical boundary theory must still identify its module category and the actual operations acting on it. The next question is how an operation can act compatibly on every module and every map between modules. That requirement leads to actions and derived centres.

    Previous5 Bar constructions and coherent operationsNext7 Actions and derived centresPointed character–action comparisons and ordinary exterior-source mapping spaces lead to different recognition theorems, with explicit residue complexes and higher compatibility questions.

    Part II Duality and centresChapter 7 of 18

    7

    Actions and derived centres

    A boundary algebra describes products of boundary fields. Recovering operations that can act on the boundary introduces a different question: how must those operations respect multiplication, changes of position and collisions? For an ordinary associative algebra, the centre answers the first part. For a chiral algebra, compatibility includes operations supported where points meet and homotopies between different ways of approaching that locus.

    Two comparison problems arise. One computes derived maps from a small exterior algebra into a vertex algebra. The other asks whether an operation on a factorizing coalgebra is determined by its value on the vacuum. Both lead to explicit rational differential forms and residues. Their conclusions concern different mapping spaces, so the map connecting those spaces must itself be constructed.

    7.1 Central operations on modules

    Let AA be a unital associative algebra over a characteristic-zero field kk. Its centre is

    Z(A)={z∈A:za=az for every a∈A}.Z(A)=\{z\in A:za=az\text{ for every }a\in A\}.

    For every left AA-module MM, a central element gives an AA-linear operator m↦zmm\mapsto zm, naturally in MM. Conversely, every natural endomorphism of the identity functor on AA-modules arises this way. Indeed, its value on the regular module is determined by z=ηA(1)z=\eta_A(1). Naturality with respect to right multiplication by aa gives az=zaaz=za; naturality with respect to A→M,b↦bmA\to M, b\mapsto bm, then gives ηM(m)=zm\eta_M(m)=zm.

    Thus the same element acts compatibly on every representation. This explains why a centre is relevant to bulk–boundary questions: an operation that can be moved without changing its interaction with boundary observables should produce compatible operators on boundary representations. Additional geometric structure is needed to turn this motivation into a statement about a field theory.

    The module interpretation also explains the derived replacement. Write Ae=A⊗kAopA^e=A\otimes_k A^{\mathrm{op}}. An AA-bimodule map A→AA\to A is determined by a central element, so

    Z(A)=HomAe⁡(A,A).Z(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_{A^e}(A,A).

    Replacing Hom by its derived functor gives the Hochschild cochain complex

    C∙(A,A)≃RHomAe⁡(A,A).C^\bullet(A,A)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{A^e}(A,A).

    For an ordinary algebra over kk, the bar resolution represents this complex by Cn(A,A)=Homk⁡(A⊗n,A)C^n(A,A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(A^{\otimes n},A). Its first differentials are

    (bz)(a)=az−za,(bf)(a1,a2)=a1f(a2)−f(a1a2)+f(a1)a2.(bz)(a)=az-za,\qquad (bf)(a_1,a_2)=a_1f(a_2)-f(a_1a_2)+f(a_1)a_2.

    Consequently HH0(A)=Z(A)HH^0(A)=Z(A), while HH1(A)HH^1(A) consists of derivations modulo inner derivations. Higher degrees retain further compatibility data.

    A class represented by a bimodule map A→A[n]A\to A[n] acts on a derived left module through

    M≃A⊗ALM⟶A[n]⊗ALM≃M[n].M\simeq A\otimes_A^L M \longrightarrow A[n]\otimes_A^L M\simeq M[n].

    Here differentials have degree +1+1, and V[1]j=Vj+1V[1]^j=V^{j+1}. The derived centre retains these operations and their coherent compositions. Hochschild cochains carry an E2E_2-algebra structure: products are accompanied by homotopies encoding their interchange. On cohomology this includes the cup product and the degree-minus-one Gerstenhaber bracket. An equivalence of underlying complexes alone does not identify those operations. See Higher Algebra, §5.3.1 and Gerstenhaber’s construction.

    For a small calculation, take A=k[x]/(x2)A=k[x]/(x^2). The ordinary centre is all of AA. A derivation is determined by f(x)=a+bxf(x)=a+bx, but

    0=f(x2)=2xf(x)=2ax0=f(x^2)=2x f(x)=2ax

    forces a=0a=0. Since AA is commutative, inner derivations vanish. Hence

    HH0(A)=k⊕︎kx,HH1(A)=kδ,δ(x)=x.HH^0(A)=k\oplus kx,\qquad HH^1(A)=k\delta, \qquad \delta(x)=x.

    The higher operation is visible even here: [δ,x]=δ(x)=x[\delta,x]=\delta(x)=x. The centre and the degree-one class do not merely coexist as vector spaces; the bracket records how the derivation acts on the central element. A list of cohomology dimensions would omit this information.

    7.2 A factorizing actor and its pointing

    Work on X=𝔸k1X=\mathbb A^1_k. A differential module is a sheaf with an action of differential operators; it keeps track of how coefficients vary with position. We use coaugmented, counital coalgebras with empty coefficient kk. A factorizing coalgebra assigns complexes of differential modules to finite labelled configurations, including their ordered collision charts. For an ordered division I=A⊔BI=A\sqcup B, its coproduct restricts on the locus where the two blocks are disjoint to an equivalence

    FI|UA,B≃(FA⊠FB)|UA,B.F_I\big|_{U_{A,B}} \simeq (F_A\boxtimes F_B)\big|_{U_{A,B}}.

    Successive divisions come with coassociativity homotopies and their higher compatibilities. Maps preserve these data, including the collision restrictions. The two orders A|BA|B and B|AB|A are distinct data unless a suitable cocommutative structure is supplied.

    We call such a coalgebra an actor when it parametrizes operations on another object. The word does not add a multiplication to FF. Two tensor products occur. Disjoint convolution, written ⋆\star, combines configurations by splitting their labels; its unit KK is concentrated at the empty configuration. The tensor ⊗!\otimes^! combines two coefficient systems at the same configuration by extraordinary pullback along the diagonal. Its unit JJ has the local unit coefficient at each configuration. A pointing is an actual coherent coalgebra map

    u:J⟶F.u:J\longrightarrow F.

    It specifies a vacuum operation together with all its compatibility homotopies. It contains more information than a class in the singleton cohomology. These conventions are those of the ordered-collision coalgebra construction, particularly its coalgebra category and diagonal tensor.

    The smallest useful test algebra has two orthogonal idempotents:

    B=kp1⊕︎kp2,pipj=δijpi.B=kp_1\oplus kp_2,\qquad p_ip_j=\delta_{ij}p_i.

    Let C=CBC=C_B be its Chevalley coalgebra: its coefficients are built from finite partitions with a BB-label on each block, and its differential merges blocks using the product of BB. It has multiplication m:C⊗!C→Cm:C\otimes^!C\to C and total unit pointing uB:J→Cu_B:J\to C. The two idempotents distinguish two colours of input and output.

    A character of (F,u)(F,u) is a coalgebra map g:F→Cg:F\to C together with a specified homotopy gu≃uBgu\simeq u_B. An action is a coalgebra map α:F⊗!C→C\alpha:F\otimes^!C\to C together with a specified homotopy α(u⊗!1C)≃1C\alpha(u\otimes^!1_C)\simeq1_C. There is no additional associative-action axiom involving a multiplication on FF. To retain the specified homotopies and homotopies between them, define the complete spaces

    𝒳(F,u)=hofibuB⁡[MapCoalg⁡(F,C)→u∗MapCoalg⁡(J,C)],𝒜C(F,u)=hofib1C⁡[MapCoalg⁡(F⊗!C,C)→(u⊗!1C)∗MapCoalg⁡(C,C)].\begin{aligned} \mathcal X(F,u) &=\operatorname{hofib}_{u_B}\left[ \operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Coalg}}(F,C) \xrightarrow{u^*}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Coalg}}(J,C)\right],\\ \mathcal A_C(F,u) &=\operatorname{hofib}_{1_C}\left[ \operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Coalg}}(F\otimes^!C,C) \xrightarrow{(u\otimes^!1_C)^*}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Coalg}}(C,C)\right]. \end{aligned}

    A homotopy fibre records a point upstairs and a path from its image to the specified base point; its higher simplices record the remaining compatibilities.

    There are explicit maps

    Θ(g)=m(g⊗!1C),Ψ(α)=α(1F⊗!uB).\Theta(g)=m(g\otimes^!1_C),\qquad \Psi(\alpha)=\alpha(1_F\otimes^!u_B).

    The first turns a character into an operation by multiplication. The second evaluates an operation on the target vacuum. The unit identity gives ΨΘ≃1\Psi\Theta\simeq1. Recognition asks whether ΘΨ≃1\Theta\Psi\simeq1 as well, on the full action space. This requires a coherent reconstruction of the operation, not only agreement on singleton values.

    A centre representing this geometric action problem would be a pointed actor ZCZ_C with a universal action, such that

    MapJ/⁡((F,u),ZC)≃𝒜C(F,u)\operatorname{Map}_{J/}\bigl((F,u),Z_C\bigr) \simeq\mathcal A_C(F,u)

    naturally for every admitted actor. Existence is part of that assertion. The binary recognition question tests whether CC, with its multiplication action, has this property on a specified family of actors. It does not identify the action problem with the Hochschild complex of the two-dimensional algebra BB.

    Derived maps can be represented using roofs

    P←≃Q⟶R,P\xleftarrow{\simeq}Q\longrightarrow R,

    where the left arrow is a weak equivalence in the category being used. A common refinement replaces QQ by another source and compares both legs. For pointed factorizing coalgebras, the pointing and the collision homotopies also belong to the diagram. For ordinary dg vertex algebras, the weak equivalences below are quasi-isomorphisms of state complexes. These two uses of roofs have different objects and weak equivalences. Comparing their mapping spaces requires a map that preserves both legs, their evaluation and their refinements.

    7.3 Recognition on Chevalley coalgebras

    Let VV be a dg chiral algebra. Its main-diagonal Chevalley coalgebra CVC_V is built from finite partitions of the labelled inputs, with a VV-coefficient on each block. Its differential combines the internal differential of VV with mergers using the chiral product. “Main-diagonal” specifies where the original one-point coefficients enter this construction; it is not a replacement by the cohomology of VV.

    Recognition theorem. Suppose VV is any unbounded dg chiral algebra over a characteristic-zero field on 𝔸1\mathbb A^1, with a genuine closed horizontal unit. For every coherent coassociative pointing u:J→CVu:J\to C_V, the maps Θ\Theta and Ψ\Psi are inverse equivalences between 𝒳(CV,u)\mathcal X(C_V,u) and 𝒜C(CV,u)\mathcal A_C(C_V,u). No homotopy from uu to the genuine unit pointing is required. The equivalence is natural under all pointed coalgebra maps between these objects, including those that preserve no chosen presentation. Arbitrary-pointing recognition.

    The proof resolves the complete mapping diagrams and filters the terms by mismatches between input and output colours. The genuine unit supplies a contraction of the absolute layers. The arbitrary pointing determines the restriction map between those layers; it is retained throughout. Taking the fibre of that restriction gives the relative layer, whose contraction includes the correction joining the two absolute contractions. At each fixed configuration only finitely many partition steps occur. This finite geometric filtration proves an equivalence of the nonlinear mapping spaces even when the coefficient complexes are unbounded. Vanishing of a tangent complex at one point would not establish the same assertion.

    There is also a module family. For an arbitrary unbounded complex MM of right differential modules, form P(M)P(M) by assigning either a unit coefficient or an MM-coefficient to each label. In a summand with several MM-labels, those labels must occupy distinct positions, and an MM-label is last in any equality block containing it. Restrict the external tensor of the assigned coefficients to that open, extend it by the direct-image functor, and sum over assignments. Projection to the summand with only unit coefficients gives P(M)→JP(M)\to J.

    For

    F=P(M)⊗!CV,h:F⟶CV,F=P(M)\otimes^!C_V,\qquad h:F\longrightarrow C_V,

    every pointing uu gives the complete projected pointing huhu. Pullback along hh identifies both character and action spaces with those of (CV,hu)(C_V,hu). Recognition therefore holds for every uu in this family. No boundedness, finite generation, holonomicity or restriction on the connection of MM is imposed. The proof contracts the positive MM-sectors as two-sided coefficient modules, rather than requiring the pointing to preserve those sectors. Radical reduction.

    A nonunital chiral algebra WW has a genuine unitization W+=W⊕︎ωXW^+=W\oplus\omega_X, where ωX\omega_X is the right differential-module unit on the curve. The inclusion gives i:CW→CW+i:C_W\to C_{W^+}, pointed upstairs by the entire composite iuiu.

    Unitization theorem. Let WW be an arbitrary unbounded, possibly noncommutative and nonconstant nonunital dg chiral algebra on 𝔸k1\mathbb A^1_k. Suppose its coherent pointing uu admits a strict closed horizontal degree-zero state a:ωX→Wa:\omega_X\to W such that

    H0(a)=H0(u1):ωX⟶H0(W).H^0(a)=H^0(u_1):\omega_X\longrightarrow H^0(W).

    Then restriction along ii induces equivalences on both complete character and action fibres. Consequently Θ\Theta and Ψ\Psi are inverse for (CW,u)(C_W,u), naturally on the full stated subcategory. The displayed equality is only in ordinary cohomology. Equality of aa and u1u_1 in full derived Hom is not a hypothesis. Unitization from an ordinary horizontal representative.

    The strict state supplies a central chain-level multiplier on W+W^+. Binary naturality of the pointing makes its action idempotent on every cohomology module. Localizing that multiplier and its complement gives actual chiral quasi-isomorphisms

    W⟶E×N,W+⟶E×N+,W\longrightarrow E\times N,\qquad W^+\longrightarrow E\times N^+,

    in a commuting square with the two unitization inclusions. Here EE is genuinely unital. The transported coherent pointings have ordinary singleton classes equal to the unit on EE and zero on N+N^+; the derived zero/unit singleton theorem promotes these particular classes to the required derived equalities. It does not replace the higher pointing cells. The split comparison then reduces both full fibres to the genuinely unital theorem. If H0(u1)=0H^0(u_1)=0, both required fibres are empty.

    For quasicoherent commutative dg 𝒪X\mathcal O_X-algebras with a compatible connection, recognition holds for every coherent pointing without this representative hypothesis. This includes all unbounded nonunital constant commutative examples, and also nonconstant examples whose ordinary singleton class has no strict horizontal representative. Thus the two results have overlapping, different domains. Commutative algebras with connection.

    7.4 Ordinary exterior sources and the map they compute

    Let 𝒱\mathcal V be the category of ordinary algebraic unital ℤ\mathbb Z-graded dg vertex superalgebras over ℂ\mathbb C, with parity given by degree modulo two, localized at maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups of the state complex. “Ordinary algebraic” means that the state spaces and tensors are the algebraic ones; no completed state product is implicit. Write dd for the internal differential and TT for translation, with dT=TddT=Td.

    For one exterior generator ϵ\epsilon of odd degree aa, with dϵ=Tϵ=0d\epsilon=T\epsilon=0, the source comparison is

    Map𝒱⁡(Λ(ϵ),B)≃Za(BhT⊗Ω∙),(BhT)j=Bj⊕︎Bj−1,\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(\Lambda(\epsilon),B) \simeq Z^a(B^{hT}\otimes\Omega_\bullet),\qquad (B^{hT})^j=B^j\oplus B^{j-1},

    where D(b,b′)=(db,Tb−db′)D(b,b')=(db,Tb-db'). Here Ωn\Omega_n is the algebra of polynomial differential forms on the standard nn-simplex. The notation ZaZ^a means closed total-degree-aa elements. A point therefore contains a closed state and a chosen homotopy killing its translation. The components are Ha(BhT)H^a(B^{hT}), and πn=Ha−n(BhT)\pi_n=H^{a-n}(B^{hT}) for n≥1n\ge1. Every odd integer aa, including negative aa, is allowed; BB can be noncommutative and unbounded. Odd-degree exterior sources.

    For two degree-one generators, mixed homotopies are essential. Put A=Λ(ϵ1,ϵ2)A=\Lambda(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2), with zero differential and translation. Define N(B)nN(B)_n as the six-tuples

    (e1,e2,u1,u2,β,ζ)∈B⊗Ωn,|ei|=1,|ui|=|β|=0,|ζ|=−1,(e_1,e_2,u_1,u_2,\beta,\zeta)\in B\otimes\Omega_n, \qquad |e_i|=1,\quad |u_i|=|\beta|=0,\quad |\zeta|=-1,

    satisfying

    dei=0,dui=Tei,dβ=u1(0)e2,dζ=Tβ−u1(0)u2.de_i=0,\qquad du_i=Te_i,\qquad d\beta=u_{1(0)}e_2,\qquad d\zeta=T\beta-u_{1(0)}u_2.

    The zero product u(0)vu_{(0)}v is the coefficient of z−1z^{-1} in Y(u,z)vY(u,z)v; dd in these equations includes the simplex differential. The uiu_i record translation homotopies, while β\beta and ζ\zeta record their mixed relation and its translation compatibility.

    Binary exterior-source theorem. The specified comparison

    ρB:Map𝒱⁡(A,B)⟶N(B)\rho_B:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(A,B)\longrightarrow N(B)

    is an equivalence for every ordinary algebraic dg vertex algebra BB, with arbitrary translation, no commutativity assumption and no boundedness assumption. Logarithmic quotient construction.

    To define this map on roofs, use the free vertex algebras on those six cells with increasing locality allowances. Their differentials are exactly the displayed equations. Each sufficiently large stage evaluates on a given finite tuple. The decisive construction supplies ordinary quotients RmR_m with specified state quasi-isomorphisms Rm→AR_m\to A and strict factorizations

    Fm+2⟶Rm+2⟶FmF_{m+2}\longrightarrow R_{m+2}\longrightarrow F_m

    of the actual free transition. This exact interpolation allows roof maps, homotopies and finite diagrams to pass through the same tuple comparison. The free stages themselves need not be quasi-isomorphic to AA; the quotients and strict transition factorization supply that comparison. The quotient is constructed from logarithmic rational forms. Its restricted dual has the de Rham differential together with collision residues; finite colour filtrations and a tensor resolution with dt=yx−xydt=yx-xy compute its cohomology. The tensor resolution leaves ordered polynomial words in every charge; the subsequent Lie and symmetric-state constructions give the four exterior classes of AA.

    For B=ℂB=\mathbb C, this theorem can be calculated directly. Translation and every zero product vanish. The three degree-zero coordinates u1,u2,βu_1,u_2,\beta are closed polynomial functions on a simplex, hence constant. The coordinate ζ\zeta vanishes because polynomial forms have no negative degree. Each eie_i is a closed one-form, and its simplicial cocycle space is K(ℂ,1)K(\mathbb C,1). Thus

    Map𝒱⁡(A,ℂ)≃ℂdisc3×K(ℂ2,1).\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(A,\mathbb C) \simeq\mathbb C^3_{\mathrm{disc}}\times K(\mathbb C^2,1).

    There is only one strict graded algebra map A→ℂA\to\mathbb C, yet the derived mapping space has these additional components and loops. They are the homotopy data carried by roofs, not further choices of the images of the degree-one generators in degree one of ℂ\mathbb C.

    The genuine Heisenberg fibre reduces to automorphisms

    The ordinary exterior-source theorem leaves a more specific action problem for the nonzero-level Heisenberg vertex algebra H=VκH=V_\kappa, κ≠0\kappa\ne0. Let B=Λ(ϵ)B=\Lambda(\epsilon), with |ϵ|=1|\epsilon|=1 and dϵ=Tϵ=0d\epsilon=T\epsilon=0. In the same ordinary dg vertex localization, retain the full actor-roof category and the genuine unit fibre

    qB:NActroof,H⁡(B)⟶F,F=hofibidH⁡[Map⁡(B⊗H,H)⟶Map⁡(H,H)].q_B:N\operatorname{Act}_{\mathrm{roof},H}(B)\longrightarrow F, \qquad F=\operatorname{hofib}_{\mathrm{id}_H} \bigl[\operatorname{Map}(B\otimes H,H) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}(H,H)\bigr].

    Both roof legs, all admitted boundary arrows and the path specifying compatibility with the unit belong to these spaces. Energy-changing arrows are included.

    The actual tuple augmentation Π:F→ℂdisc2×K(ℂ,1)\Pi:F\to\mathbb C^2_{\mathrm{disc}}\times K(\mathbb C,1) has weak-equivalence composite ΠqB\Pi q_B. It therefore computes the source and its detected image. Convolution and the actual roof translations further give

    F≃ℂdisc2×F0,F\simeq\mathbb C^2_{\mathrm{disc}}\times F^0,

    where F0F^0 is the whole zero sector of the charge and constant detector. This sector is not known to be connected.

    There is now a description of the remaining based fibre using actual automorphisms. Form the square-zero extension

    X1=H⊕︎ϵ1H,|ϵ1|=1,ϵ12=dϵ1=Tϵ1=0,X_1=H\oplus\epsilon_1H, \qquad |\epsilon_1|=1, \quad \epsilon_1^2=d\epsilon_1=T\epsilon_1=0,

    with its canonical section and projection. Work in the genuine pointed slice 𝒱H//H\mathcal V_{H//H}, which retains both the under-HH and over-HH homotopies. Let UU be the space of its automorphisms of X1X_1 that induce the identity on state cohomology. At the trivial action α0\alpha_0, define

    Φ=hofib0⁡[Fα0→δK(ℂ,1)],\Phi=\operatorname{hofib}_0 \bigl[F_{\alpha_0}\xrightarrow{\delta}K(\mathbb C,1)\bigr],

    where Fα0F_{\alpha_0} is the connected component of α0\alpha_0. The scalar section makes Φ\Phi connected, and the genuine loop comparison gives

    U≃ΩΦ,qB is an equivalence⟺F0 is connected and U is contractible.U\simeq\Omega\Phi, \qquad q_B\text{ is an equivalence} \Longleftrightarrow F^0\text{ is connected and }U\text{ is contractible}.

    This is an exact reduction of the original problem; neither condition on the right is established. Genuine fibre reduction.

    The two requirements measure different possible defects. Based loops test extra automorphisms in the component of the trivial action, but they cannot detect another component of the whole zero sector. Nor can endomorphism composition be replaced by loop addition: composition multiplies the detected scalars and has identity scalar 11, while loop concatenation adds scalars and has identity 00. The proved splitting is a statement about spaces over the scalar set, with no product decomposition for composition. The remaining equivalence.

    7.5 Residues with spectators

    Adding fixed field insertions to the source produces rational forms with spectators: labelled positions z1,…,zrz_1,\ldots,z_r that remain as parameters while auxiliary marked positions w1,…,wmw_1,\ldots,w_m are differentiated or absorbed by residues. Three sets of nonnegative integer bounds control the poles: NijN_{ij} for spectator pairs, bjb_j for a marked point meeting spectator jj, and a positive odd integer μ\mu for marked pairs.

    Here is the rational complex to which the strict vanishing results apply. Choose a subset S⊆{1,…,r}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\} of selected spectators, put s=|S|s=|S|, and fix the charge q=m+sq=m+s. A degree-ii form in the marked variables contributes to total degree n=2s+in=2s+i. It is anti-invariant under permutations of the marked variables, acting on both coefficients and differentials. The coefficient of dwIdw_I has the following pole bounds:

    divisormaximum pole orderwa=wbμ+𝟏{a,b}∩I≠⌀wa=zjbj+𝟏a∈I(j∉S)wa=zj2bj+μ+1+𝟏a∈I(j∈S)zi=zjNij(|{i,j}∩S|=0)zi=zjNij+bi+bj+1(|{i,j}∩S|=1)zi=zjNij+2bi+2bj+μ+2(|{i,j}∩S|=2).\begin{array}{c|c} \text{divisor}&\text{maximum pole order}\\ \hline w_a=w_b&\mu+\mathbf1_{\{a,b\}\cap I\ne\varnothing}\\ w_a=z_j&b_j+\mathbf1_{a\in I}\quad(j\notin S)\\ w_a=z_j&2b_j+\mu+1+\mathbf1_{a\in I}\quad(j\in S)\\ z_i=z_j&N_{ij}\quad(|\{i,j\}\cap S|=0)\\ z_i=z_j&N_{ij}+b_i+b_j+1\quad(|\{i,j\}\cap S|=1)\\ z_i=z_j&N_{ij}+2b_i+2b_j+\mu+2\quad(|\{i,j\}\cap S|=2). \end{array}

    No other poles are allowed. A total-degree-nn family is Φ=(ϕS)S\Phi=(\phi_S)_S, where ϕS\phi_S is a form of degree n−2|S|n-2|S| in q−|S|q-|S| marked variables satisfying the displayed bounds. A component is zero unless 0≤n−2|S|≤q−|S|0\le n-2|S|\le q-|S|. For every i≠ji\ne j, i∈Si\in S, j∉Sj\notin S, put S′=(S∖{i})∪{j}S'=(S\setminus\{i\})\cup\{j\}. The additional relation is, coefficientwise,

    ϕS+εS;i,jϕS′has pole order at most Nij along zi=zj.\phi_S+\varepsilon_{S;i,j}\phi_{S'} \quad\text{has pole order at most }N_{ij}\text{ along }z_i=z_j.
    (R)

    To define the sign, let θ1,…,θr\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r be anticommuting symbols and write θS\theta_S for their product in increasing order. Using a common anticommuting symbol θ\theta, set εS;i,j∈{1,−1}\varepsilon_{S;i,j}\in\{1,-1\} by

    θS|θi=θ=εS;i,jθS′|θj=θ.\left.\theta_S\right|_{\theta_i=\theta} =\varepsilon_{S;i,j} \left.\theta_{S'}\right|_{\theta_j=\theta}.

    For |S|=1|S|=1, relation (R) says that ϕ{i}+ϕ{j}\phi_{\{i\}}+\phi_{\{j\}} has pole order at most NijN_{ij} along zi=zjz_i=z_j. The relation couples the components associated with the two possible selected spectator labels.

    Denote the resulting complex by Dr,q(b,N;μ)D_{r,q}(b,N;\mu). Its differential is marked de Rham differentiation plus the signed residues Resw=zj⁡\operatorname{Res}_{w=z_j}, which convert a marked variable into a selected spectator. A residue lowers form degree by one and increases ss by one, so both differential terms raise 2s+i2s+i by one. The left-residue convention, extracting the indicated dwdw first, makes these terms anticommute.

    The charge-one case explains why the charge restriction in the theorem below matters. With one spectator and N=0N=0, put y=w−zy=w-z. The complex is

    y−bℂ[z,y]→dyy−b−1ℂ[z,y]dy→Resy=0⁡ℂ[z].y^{-b}\mathbb C[z,y] \xrightarrow{d_y} y^{-b-1}\mathbb C[z,y]\,dy \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Res}_{y=0}} \mathbb C[z].

    A Laurent monomial yjdyy^jdy has the primitive yj+1/(j+1)y^{j+1}/(j+1) unless j=−1j=-1; the allowed bound puts that primitive in the first term. The missing monomial dy/ydy/y maps to 11 under the residue. Hence the last two cohomology groups vanish, while H0=ℂ[z]H^0=\mathbb C[z]. For several spectators the analogous surviving module is

    MN(r)=(∏i<j(zi−zj)−Nij)ℂ[z1,…,zr].M_N(r)=\left(\prod_{i<j}(z_i-z_j)^{-N_{ij}}\right) \mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_r].

    It survives at q=1q=1, independently of μ\mu.

    Strict three-spectator theorem. For r=3r=3, every bj,Nij≥0b_j,N_{ij}\ge0, every positive odd μ\mu, and every charge q≥2q\ge2,

    Hn(D3,q(b,N;μ))=0(n<q).H^n(D_{3,q}(b,N;\mu))=0\qquad(n<q).

    This holds over the whole polynomial spectator base, including simultaneous collisions, and in every homogeneity. The conclusion Hn=0H^n=0 for q≥2q\ge2 and n<qn<q, with positive odd μ\mu, also holds for r=2r=2 and arbitrary nonnegative b,Nb,N, and for arbitrary rr when every bj=0b_j=0 and Nij≥0N_{ij}\ge0. A further total theorem gives Hn(D4,5)=0H^n(D_{4,5})=0 for n<5n<5, with b=(1,1,1,1)b=(1,1,1,1), μ=1\mu=1 and arbitrary Nij≥0N_{ij}\ge0. Three-spectator proof; four-spectator charge-five proof.

    For three spectators, filter by the selected count ss. The associated graded differential is marked de Rham differentiation. The columns at s=0,1,2,3s=0,1,2,3 have lower total-degree bounds q−1,q,q,q+2q-1,q,q,q+2. These are lower bounds, not assertions that a nonzero term occurs there: absent columns and nonnegative form degree raise the actual starts at small qq. Only the unselected column can contribute below qq. Its possible degree-q−1q-1 class maps injectively under the actual first residue into the constrained one-selected column, so it disappears. The filtration is finite, which gives convergence to the original total complex without a completion argument.

    The column bounds require more than pole counting. They use exact image ideals, their intersections along collision strata, and the differential-module connections. Multiplication by the common spectator factor ∏(zi−zj)Nij\prod(z_i-z_j)^{N_{ij}} then identifies the prescribed rational modules with their N=0N=0 versions. This is a chain isomorphism between those modules, not an assertion that the factor is a unit in the polynomial base.

    There is a uniform statement for the first compatibility of pairwise data. Let r≥1,m≥0r\ge1,m\ge0, all bj=1b_j=1, μ=1\mu=1, and Nij=0N_{ij}=0. Over S=ℂ[z1,…,zr,c1,…,cm]S=\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_r,c_1,\ldots,c_m], set

    P(X)=Xm+c1Xm−1+⋯+cm,tij=zj−zi,Δ=∏i<jtij3,Gi=P(zi)3,Fi=(∏a<b, i∉{a,b}tab3)∏j≠iGj,𝔞=(F1,…,Fr).\begin{gathered} P(X)=X^m+c_1X^{m-1}+\cdots+c_m,\qquad t_{ij}=z_j-z_i,\\ \Delta=\prod_{i<j}t_{ij}^3,\qquad G_i=P(z_i)^3,\\ F_i=\left(\prod_{a<b,\ i\notin\{a,b\}}t_{ab}^3\right) \prod_{j\ne i}G_j,\qquad \mathfrak a=(F_1,\ldots,F_r). \end{gathered}

    For m=0m=0, take P=1P=1. The literal identity

    ⋂i<j(𝔞,tij3)=(𝔞,Δ)\bigcap_{i<j}(\mathfrak a,t_{ij}^3)=(\mathfrak a,\Delta)

    says that compatible pairwise principal parts in the specified image modules arise from a single joint source. Its proof uses the actual coefficient lattice, whose projective dimension is at most two for m≥2m\ge2, and induction along collision partitions with the outside polynomial factors retained. The identity establishes this first compatibility; it does not establish the second compatibility or total vanishing for arbitrary rr. First compatibility defect.

    The strict inequality cannot be replaced by n≤qn\le q at fixed bounds. With r=2r=2, q=4q=4, b=(1,1)b=(1,1), N12=0N_{12}=0 and μ=1\mu=1, the rational complex has a nonzero class in H4H^4. Such a class may die after the pole bounds are enlarged. A fixed-bound counterexample and an eventual comparison through larger bounds are therefore different mathematical statements. The fixed-bound residue class.

    7.6 The remaining comparison

    The geometric action problem also has concrete higher homotopies. For arbitrary unbounded coassociative actors, the prescribed three-block pointed boundary has a filling with its original root, marks and scalar pointing retained. Its construction uses two genuine vacuum labels, their proper deletion edges and full differential-module residue maps; it cancels the action-generated residue without declaring the entire normal kernel contractible. No cocommutativity assumption is needed. Three-block filling.

    A separate comparison of two prescribed mixed primitives holds on the old separated locus z0≠z1z_0\ne z_1 when the underlying FF has a supplied coherent cocommutative structure. The action and pointing themselves need only be coassociative. It fills the specified closed difference and its corner restriction; it does not extend across the old collision diagonal. These hypotheses must remain distinct from those of the three-block theorem. Separated-base primitive comparison.

    Recognition for arbitrary pointed factorizing actors still asks for Θ\Theta to be an equivalence with all changes of roots, collision restrictions and arbitrarily long refined words. The constructions above provide particular parts of that comparison. They do not supply the whole family. Likewise, the ordinary binary exterior-source theorem computes its stated vertex-algebra mapping space; a comparison with the geometric action space must additionally preserve the original actor, both roof legs, evaluation and every required incoming refinement. For sources with further generators and spectators, exact interpolation must still be constructed in that full scope.

    These questions force attention to the spaces on which operations can be composed. A residue map defined on algebraic rational forms, a homotopy on a separated configuration and an operation on a completed space of fields have different domains. Passing between them requires the specified tensor, support and completion maps. Those maps are the subject of the next chapter.

    Part III Operations and their domainsChapter 8 of 18

    8

    Tensor products, support and completion

    An operation on every finite collection of states need not act on an infinite state. The difficulty can occur before any integral diverges: the proposed output may simply lie outside the vector space on which the next operation is defined. For boundary reconstruction this matters twice. Several incoming representations must first be combined, and the resulting object must then be compared with a space of current operations. These constructions involve different infinite sums. Their order determines the comparison map.
