    (17.1)

    form an adjunction. Derived categories are used with their mapping complexes, as in Chapter 6. The right BB-action on PP produces the left BB-action on the Hom complex by precomposition. The actual unit and counit are

    ηL:L⟶GF(L),εM:FG(M)⟶M.\eta_L:L\longrightarrow GF(L), \qquad \varepsilon_M:FG(M)\longrightarrow M.
    (17.2)

    They compare the original object with the result of passing through the interface and back. If all units are equivalences, FF is fully faithful. The counit then identifies which objects of D(A)D(A) it reconstructs. Full faithfulness is already a reconstruction theorem on the image; equivalence with the whole target category requires that image to be the whole category.

    For a complete finite example, take A=Mn(k)A=M_n(k), B=kB=k, P=knP=k^n, and let EijE_{ij} be the matrix units. Put e=E11e=E_{11}. Then G(M)=eMG(M)=eM, and the counit is

    εM:kn⊗eM⟶M,vi⊗m⟼Ei1m.\varepsilon_M:k^n\otimes eM\longrightarrow M, \qquad v_i\otimes m\longmapsto E_{i1}m.
    (17.3)

    Its inverse is

    M⟶kn⊗eM,m⟼∑ivi⊗E1im.M\longrightarrow k^n\otimes eM, \qquad m\longmapsto\sum_i v_i\otimes E_{1i}m.

    The two composites are identities because E1jEi1=δijeE_{1j}E_{i1}=\delta_{ij}e and ∑iEi1E1i=1A\sum_iE_{i1}E_{1i}=1_A. The unit sends a vector vv to v1⊗vv_1\otimes v in e(kn⊗V)e(k^n\otimes V), so it is also an isomorphism. This proves the equivalence of module categories directly, including its maps.

    The same example shows why a centre alone is insufficient. The algebra of upper triangular two-by-two matrices over kk has centre kk, just as M2(k)M_2(k) does. It has two nonisomorphic simple modules, obtained by evaluating the two diagonal entries; M2(k)M_2(k) has one simple module up to isomorphism. Their module categories are not equivalent. A centre comparison and an interface equivalence answer different questions.

    In a field theory, PP is not an arbitrary bimodule selected to make (17.2) invertible. It must come from the prescribed line, junction or boundary condition. Its action, support and differential are part of the comparison. The finite matrix example gives the criterion to test; it does not identify any physical interface with knk^n.

    17.2 What the affine theorem reconstructs

    Chapter 6 constructs this kind of comparison for the line algebra B=Y−s(𝔰𝔩3)B=Y_{-s}(\mathfrak{sl}_3), with s∈ℂ∖ℚs\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q, and affine raw level s−3s-3, with invariant form κ(x,y)=Tr⁡(xy)\kappa(x,y)=\operatorname{Tr}(xy). The induced object

    W=As−3⊗U(t𝔰𝔩3[t])ℂW=A_{s-3}\otimes_{U(t\mathfrak{sl}_3[t])}\mathbb C

    has a horizontal regular representation at energy zero. The generator action on its Chevalley resolution, including the correction to right multiplication, specifies the line action used in the adjunction.

    Under the smooth realization hypotheses stated in that chapter—its prescribed right action, homogeneous endomorphism comparison, Taylor-resolution coherences and enhanced tensor–Hom adjunction—the original unit is invertible on every ordinary unbounded BB-complex. Internal energy can be forgotten or retained with arbitrary algebraic support. The resulting equivalence is

    D(B)≃𝒞,𝒞=Loc⁡(W)D(B)\simeq\mathscr C, \qquad \mathscr C=\operatorname{Loc}(W)
    (17.4)

    in the ungraded case; in the graded case all energy shifts of WW generate 𝒞\mathscr C. Here Loc⁡\operatorname{Loc} means closure under shifts, cones, arbitrary coproducts and retracts inside the given smooth derived category. The actual counit ΦΨM→M\Phi\Psi M\to M is the coreflection into this subcategory.

    The reach to unbounded complexes has an algebraic explanation. With R=U(𝔰𝔩3)R=U(\mathfrak{sl}_3) and positive-weight ideal II,

    I⊗R𝐋4=0,I⊗R𝐋3≠0.I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}4}=0, \qquad I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}3}\ne0.
    (17.5)

    The finite descent tower reduces every source to four unrestricted inflated RR-complexes. The cofree calculation already identifies the actual unit on those complexes. Finite triangles then extend that same natural transformation to every source. An unproved interchange of an infinite coproduct with the right adjoint is unnecessary.

    This result retains several useful boundaries. It does not identify 𝒞\mathscr C with every smooth affine object. It also does not identify the coreflection with the derived joint-torsion functor. Chapter 6 gives an unbounded positive-current example where the torsion adjunction has an additional product-modulo-sum class and fails to be fully faithful. At other affine levels, actual realization kernels coexist with the valid finite-stage unit. At raw 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 level −3-3, a different telescope survives realization but is killed by the weight-zero quotient; it obstructs that descent route, not realization itself.

    The reconstruction theorem therefore identifies a precise category through a precise interface. To identify a separately defined physical boundary functor with this one, its action and right adjoint must be compared on the original complexes. Agreement of ordinary endomorphism algebras or of cohomology dimensions does not supply that comparison. The inflated-coefficient theorem for every simple type and every level remains available on its stated inputs, independently of whether a full-unit theorem holds there.

    17.3 Products must survive passage through the interface

    An equivalence of linear categories can forget the way systems combine. If 𝒞\mathcal C and 𝒟\mathcal D have specified tensor products, a monoidal comparison includes maps

    γL,M:F(L)⊗𝒟F(M)⟶F(L⊗𝒞M)\gamma_{L,M}:F(L)\otimes_{\mathcal D}F(M) \longrightarrow F(L\otimes_{\mathcal C}M)
    (17.6)

    and a unit comparison. Their associativity square compares the two maps obtained from three inputs, and the unit diagrams compare insertion of the tensor unit. A strong monoidal functor requires these maps to be equivalences. A braided comparison also includes the exchange square and its compatibility with the associator.

    For local fields, the two tensor products in (17.6) may depend on positions and expansions. Chapter 12 supplies a complete positive example in the spectral class: the form ρz\rho_z defines fields, their exchange, the cross-contracted tensor product, and a level-indexed coproduct preserving the fields. The field hexagon is an identity on a stated Laurent expansion space. This is substantially more information than an abstract coproduct on state vectors.

    Chapter 8 supplies another positive result. For nonrational 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2, under its realization and finite-descent hypotheses, every finite tuple of ordinary unbounded line modules has a comparison with the independently defined radial current complex. Scalar extension to the shape field FF occurs before completion to F((q))F((q)). Rational evaluation and its affine restriction preserve the outgoing action and all stated incoming actions. Composition of the original kernels along a finite tree agrees on this common radial domain.

    That conclusion does not define substitution on every separately completed intermediate tensor. The series

    ∑n≥0qnλ−n2\sum_{n\geq0}q^n\lambda^{-n^2}

    is a valid element of ℂ(λ)((q))\mathbb C(\lambda)((q)), whereas substituting λ=zq\lambda=zq produces outer orders n−n2n-n^2 with no lower bound. The proposed substituted series is outside the iterated Laurent space. A larger tensor comparison must impose and prove the support estimates that exclude this failure, or choose a different independently justified domain.

    Likewise, an integral collision fibre cannot be obtained by setting the discriminant to zero in a space where it has been inverted. The finite integral heads in Chapter 8 carry actual derived collision maps before localization. Comparing those maps with the radial theorem requires the finite-head and completion comparisons together. A common formal expression is not a common domain.

    Native fields on every algebraic input

    The native four-colour construction has a dg quantum vertex structure on every algebraic input through the coefficient ring

    R3=ℂ[ℏ]/(ℏ3).R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3).

    Its state complex is M3=VKB(𝔤𝔩2)⊗R3F0M_3=V^{KB}(\mathfrak{gl}_2)\otimes_{R_3}F_0, with the trace-current and trace-ghost factors retained. At every numerical level KK, including 00 and −2-2, the field 𝕐−\mathbb Y_-, translation, vacuum and exchange give a dg quantum vertex superalgebra on all algebraic states. The locality exponent depends on the first two states and works for every final state. The opposite field 𝕐+\mathbb Y_+ is a weakly associative chain field, joined to 𝕐−\mathbb Y_- by the specified field homotopy. A separate full quantum vertex structure for the opposite exchange is not part of this conclusion. All-input field theorem.

    Passing to cohomology removes the exchange correction. The exchange has an algebraically finite Laurent homotopy

    [dM⊗,Λ(u)]=SM(u)−1.[d_M^{\otimes},\Lambda(u)]=S_M(u)-1.

    For cycle representatives of the first two inputs, one power of the separation clears its poles. The difference of the two exchanged products then becomes a coefficientwise boundary for every final cycle. Consequently H∙(M3,dM)H^\bullet(M_3,d_M) carries an ordinary local vertex superalgebra, with R3R_3-bilinear fields and the original faithful central R3R_3-action. Both ordered fields induce that same operation. The argument needs no Künneth identification over R3R_3, and ordinary locality does not make the singular products zero. Cohomology fields.

    There is a separate computation of the states at each fixed K≠−2K\ne-2. An algebraic chain frame preserves the native minimal inclusion and identifies

    H∙(M3)≅(R3𝟏⊕︎R3[ωℏ])⊗ℂ(ℂ[I1,I2,…]⊗Λ(ξ0I,ξ1I,…)),|ωℏ|=3.H^\bullet(M_3)\cong (R_3\mathbf1\oplus R_3[\omega_\hbar]) \otimes_{\mathbb C} \left(\mathbb C[I_1,I_2,\ldots] \otimes\Lambda(\xi^I_0,\xi^I_1,\ldots)\right), \qquad |\omega_\hbar|=3.

    The trace factor has zero differential. This is an identification of state cohomology; a presentation of all its vertex products requires the corresponding field calculation. The frame is chosen at the fixed numerical level and is not asserted to continue through K=−2K=-2. At that critical level, algebraic current-invariant states tensored with the ghost vacuum give a free submodule of H0H^0, including the classical Sugawara state. Exhaustion of critical cohomology and critical physical evaluation remain further questions.

    Retained kernels and the first rooted comparison

    A scalar field forgets its ghost output. A retained kernel keeps that output until it is paired with a coefficient functional. Let V=M30V=M_3^0, let 𝒢\mathcal G be the completed ghost algebra, and let IˆL\widehat I_L be its closed left ideal generated by ghost modes of index at least LL. Put FL=𝒢/IˆLF_L=\mathcal G/\widehat I_L. A retained kernel of degree nn assigns to each algebraic current state w∈Vw\in V a compatible Laurent series

    TL(w)∈(V⊗FLn)((u)).T_L(w)\in(V\otimes F_L^n)((u)).

    These R3R_3-linear families form the retained kernel space ℰretn\mathcal E^n_{\rm ret} for n≥0n\ge0; put ℰretn=0\mathcal E^n_{\rm ret}=0 for n<0n<0. Their Laurent lower bound may depend on LL and ww. The combined current–ghost differential 𝒟\mathscr D on these kernels squares to zero. The ghost differential itself is evaluated at a larger cutoff before projection; the individual FLF_L are not thereby dg quotient algebras. A retained cochain has an additional state input: in degree jj it belongs to

    𝒬ret,j=∏p≥0HomR3⁡(M3p,ℰretp+j),δΨ=𝒟Ψ−(−1)jΨdM.\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{ret},j} =\prod_{p\ge0}\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3} \bigl(M_3^p,\mathcal E^{p+j}_{\rm ret}\bigr), \qquad \delta\Psi=\mathscr D\Psi-(-1)^j\Psi d_M.

    Thus Ψ(x)\Psi(x) is a retained kernel on the current input ww, with output ghost degree p+jp+j when x∈M3px\in M_3^p.

    At every numerical KK, the dressed field gives a retained cocycle 𝒴−\mathcal Y_-. The restricted exchange homotopy gives a second cocycle 𝒴♯\mathcal Y^\sharp, with the opposite scalar field; its polarization agrees with 𝕐+\mathbb Y_+ up to a coboundary in the kernel of the corner projection. Write AcurA_{\rm cur} for the full smooth native current algebra and Acur,RA_{{\rm cur},R} for its specified right quotients. Coefficient pairing defines continuous dg AcurA_{\rm cur}-bimodule evaluations on the ordered rooted carrier

    Nrt1−n=lim←R⁡colimL≥1⁡(HomR3⁡(FLn,Acur)⊗R3,algAcur,R).N_{\rm rt}^{1-n} =\varprojlim_R\operatorname*{colim}_{L\ge1} \left(\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(F_L^n,A_{\rm cur}) \otimes_{R_3,\mathrm{alg}}A_{{\rm cur},R}\right).

    These source coefficients are independent of uu. At each right quotient they have one middle ghost cutoff and finite right PBW support; neither is required to be uniform over all right quotients. The recipient is the shifted scalar Hom complex

    Q3=HomR3⁡(M3,HomR3⁡(V,V((u))))[−1],Q_3=\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3} \bigl(M_3,\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(V,V((u)))\bigr)[-1],

    with the pointwise Laurent topology in its two algebraic inputs. Its Laurent floor need not be uniform over all inputs. Homogeneity supplies the finite ghost box and Laurent floor needed for the pairing. The two evaluations E♭,E♯:Nrt→Q3E^\flat,E^\sharp:N_{\rm rt}\to Q_3 retain both endpoint actions and both translation identities, and an actual bimodule homotopy joins them. At K=−2K=-2 they are new rooted maps defined by the field, not an extension of the noncritical marked evaluation. Retained kernels and rooted evaluations.

    At a fixed K≠−2K\ne-2, including K=0K=0, let E3E_3 be the prescribed pure-root evaluation, with retained cochain Φ∈𝒬ret,0\Phi\in\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{ret},0}, and put Δ=Φ−𝒴♯\Delta=\Phi-\mathcal Y^\sharp. Their scalar kernels agree. Use the translation-compatible state retract with its full trace factor: if ii and pp are its inclusion and projection, its degree-minus-one homotopy kk satisfies dMk+kdM=1−ipd_Mk+kd_M=1-ip. Write Δ1\Delta_1 for the restriction to inserted ghost degree one. The degree-minus-one retained cochain

    κ(1)|M32=Δ1k|M32,κ(1)|M3p=0(p≠2)\kappa^{(1)}|_{M_3^2}=\Delta_1k|_{M_3^2}, \qquad \kappa^{(1)}|_{M_3^p}=0\quad(p\ne2)

    has zero scalar pairing and obeys both translation laws. With δ\delta the retained Hom differential,

    𝒴♯,1=𝒴♯+δκ(1)\mathcal Y^{\sharp,1}=\mathcal Y^\sharp+\delta\kappa^{(1)}

    agrees with Φ\Phi on inserted ghost degrees zero and one. The induced evaluation therefore agrees with E3E_3 on the subcomplex of middle degrees at most one, and is globally homotopic to the evaluation defined by 𝒴♯\mathcal Y^\sharp on NrtN_{\rm rt}. The first rooted comparison.

    The contraction explains why this correction exists. Its degree-one small image consists of trace-current polynomials times one trace ghost. The two kernels agree there, while the cocycle identity makes Δ1d=0\Delta_1d=0 on degree zero. The contraction identity then gives Δ1=Δ1kd\Delta_1=\Delta_1kd. The full trace factor is essential to this argument.

    Zero scalar pairing fixes the scalar normalization. The correction is not asserted to start at order ℏ2\hbar^2 or to preserve the strict creation column. Higher retained degrees, positive inserted marked degree, the original coefficient-valued Laurent source and the three unit-cone comparisons remain separate. In the larger source, one ghost cutoff, one Laurent floor and finite right support must govern a whole series at each right quotient. The pointwise pairing above does not supply those whole-series estimates or a physical tensorator.

    The endpoint obstruction has a specified acting algebra

    The intrinsic field theorem can coexist with an obstruction to a physical coefficient comparison because the latter must preserve an additional action. Write V=M30V=M_3^0 for the ghost-degree-zero state module and A3A_3 for its prescribed current algebra. Let

    A=EndR3≥0⁡(M3)×EndR3⁡(V)A3,q:A⟶A3,A=\operatorname{End}^{\ge0}_{R_3}(M_3) \times_{\operatorname{End}_{R_3}(V)}A_3, \qquad q:A\longrightarrow A_3,

    be the actual dg fibre product, whose endomorphisms raise ghost degree by a nonnegative integer. Inflate the marked source 𝒩3[1]\mathcal N_3[1] along qq. The exact corner sequence, with kernel 𝒦\mathcal K, is a sequence of dg AA-bimodules, but it has no global chain section. The kernel of qq contains a closed trace creator cc, with c2=0c^2=0, which kills the source unit class. On every closed normalized bulk lift GG of the prescribed scalar class,

    G(𝟏,𝟏)=𝟏,[cG](𝟏,𝟏)=[ξ0I]≠0.G(\mathbf1,\mathbf1)=\mathbf1, \qquad [cG](\mathbf1,\mathbf1)=[\xi^I_0]\ne0.

    Thus the source unit and its required image cannot have the same cc-action.

    At every fixed K≠−2K\ne-2, the two ordered marked evaluations have the same nonzero derived obstruction:

    βAE3[1]=βAE3[1]≠0inHomD(Ae)⁡(𝒩3[1],𝒦[1]).\beta_AE_3[1]=\beta_A\overline E_3[1]\ne0 \quad\text{in}\quad \operatorname{Hom}_{D(A^e)} \bigl(\mathcal N_3[1],\mathcal K[1]\bigr).

    Restriction to the exterior algebra generated by cc detects a split free cyclic R3R_3-submodule. An equivalent resolution of the same source module cannot remove the obstruction, nor can standard uncurved A∞A_\infty-bimodule coherence. This excludes the specified quotient-inflated lift. A replacement action, acting algebra or recipient must come with a comparison preserving the original operations. The exact endpoint obstruction.

    The trace detector has a stronger module-theoretic form in a specified corner complex. Put F1M3=M3≥1F^1M_3=M_3^{\ge1}. Let ℬ\mathcal B be the subcomplex of two-input Laurent cochains

    HomR3⁡(M3⊗M3,M3((u)))\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(M_3\otimes M_3,M_3((u)))

    whose value lies in (F1M3)((u))(F^1M_3)((u)) whenever the rooted, second input lies in F1M3F^1M_3. Let 𝒦⊂ℬ\mathcal K\subset\mathcal B consist of cochains whose every output lies in (F1M3)((u))(F^1M_3)((u)). The corner map

    π:ℬ⟶𝒞=HomR3⁡(M3⊗V,V((u)))\pi:\mathcal B\longrightarrow \mathcal C=\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(M_3\otimes V,V((u)))

    restricts the rooted input to its ghost-free part V=M30V=M_3^0 and projects the output to ghost degree zero; its kernel is 𝒦\mathcal K.

    For a closed G∈ℬ0G\in\mathcal B^0 with [πG]=[W±][\pi G]=[W_\pm], multiplication of its output by exterior trace monomials gives a split copy of ΛR3(ξ0I,ξ1I,…)\Lambda_{R_3}(\xi^I_0,\xi^I_1,\ldots) in H∙(ℬ)H^\bullet(\mathcal B); its positive-degree part splits into H∙(𝒦)H^\bullet(\mathcal K). This is a splitting of graded R3R_3-modules, not a presentation of a product on Hom cohomology. Suppose a dg acting algebra preserves this corner exact sequence and contains a closed degree-one element acting by output multiplication by a trace ghost. If a dg module map from SS to 𝒞\mathcal C sends a closed degree-zero element to the normalized scalar class [W±][W_\pm] and H1(S)=0H^1(S)=0, it has no lift to ℬ\mathcal B in the derived module category or as a standard uncurved A∞A_\infty-module map. The trace creator kills the source class and cannot kill its required image. The acting-algebra and diagram hypotheses are essential; this obstruction does not exclude the retained-kernel pairing or a relative cone with different cohomology. Trace classes and the source-degree obstruction.

    The noncritical marked evaluations themselves remain positive constructions. Their endpoint-bilinear homotopy restores the reversed scalar field, both Ward laws, the prescribed minimal pairings and the proper unit-cone diagrams. A separate scalar correction also aligns the two scalar homotopies while preserving translation. Scalar connecting classes can therefore vanish while the derived bimodule obstruction survives. Throughout, the coefficient source retains one Laurent floor, one ghost cutoff and finite right PBW support across each whole series at a fixed right quotient and algebraic inserted input. The independent physical right adjoint, its counit, both products and tensorator still require maps on that declared domain.

    17.4 A bulk action and a universal centre

    In the ordinary associative case, Hochschild cochains

    C∙(B,B)=RHomB⊗Bop⁡(B,B)C^\bullet(B,B)=R\operatorname{Hom}_{B\otimes B^{\mathrm{op}}}(B,B)

    act coherently on derived BB-modules. This suggests a place for bulk observables that act compatibly on all boundary systems. In chiral geometry, however, the appropriate action problem includes the configuration opens, the tensor products, the pointing and the collision homotopies. Its representing object need not be the Hochschild complex of a two-dimensional test algebra.

    Chapter 7 defines one such geometric problem exactly. A pointed factorizing coalgebra (F,u)(F,u) is tested against the Chevalley coalgebra CC of the two-idempotent algebra. The complete character and action spaces are 𝒳(F,u)\mathcal X(F,u) and 𝒜C(F,u)\mathcal A_C(F,u). Multiplication and vacuum evaluation give

    Θ:𝒳(F,u)⟶𝒜C(F,u),Ψ:𝒜C(F,u)⟶𝒳(F,u),ΨΘ≃1.\Theta:\mathcal X(F,u)\longrightarrow\mathcal A_C(F,u), \qquad \Psi:\mathcal A_C(F,u)\longrightarrow\mathcal X(F,u), \qquad \Psi\Theta\simeq1.
    (17.7)

    Recognition asks whether the other composite is homotopic to the identity with all the required compatibilities. This is proved for the full families stated in Chapter 7: arbitrary pointings on genuinely unital Chevalley coalgebras, their specified module extensions, and the nonunital families covered by the horizontal-representative or commutative-connection theorems. The three-block filling for arbitrary coassociative actors requires no cocommutativity. The separate old-base closed-corner comparison has its own coherent cocommutativity hypothesis and remains on the separated locus.

    A universal geometric centre would represent the action space for every admitted pointed actor. Even if such representability is established, a bulk reconstruction still needs a map from the independently defined bulk observables to that centre. It must identify the actual action, its product and its support. The ordinary exterior-source mapping-space theorem is another exact positive result; it does not define this geometric bulk map by changing the name of its target.

    There is also an accomplished classical geometric reconstruction. Chapter 13 constructs the complete ordinary coefficient-family system of a fixed unital chiral algebra, with arbitrary classical parameter schemes, compatible vacuum insertions and collision equivalences. Realizing the vacuum and applying the geometric residue construction returns the original chiral algebra. This theorem explains what additional geometric information makes reconstruction possible. Its ordinary tensors and fixed algebra are part of its scope; its conclusion does not assert a derived reconstruction of an interacting bulk theory.

    17.5 States and amplitudes impose another comparison

    Return to the Gaussian of Chapter 1. Normalization produces a linear functional ω\omega with ω(1)=1\omega(1)=1. The unnormalized functional has the form

    Z(O)=Z(1)ω(O).Z(O)=Z(1)\,\omega(O).
    (17.8)

    Knowing ω\omega leaves the factor Z(1)Z(1) undetermined. If that factor varies in a line rather than as a scalar, one must also identify the line and its connection. This distinction survives when the finite integral becomes a field theory.

    Chapter 11 constructs a numerical normalized Gaussian on the original continued source graph. Its domain includes the fixed metric and density, 0<|q|<10<|q|<1, κ≠0\kappa\ne0, ℏ>0\hbar>0, a smooth integrable source in the stated small inverse neighbourhood, zero normal trace, and a supplied smooth Ward filling TμT_\mu. The even finite-cycle fields converge to a Radon Gaussian; the complete odd and mixed moments are given by the graded Wick rule. Odd variables are not assigned an ordinary probability law.

    The original weighted coefficient heat construction gives another object: a based local vacuum line with a nonzero finite-part section. It uses its own reflected realization, spectral gap, smooth source bounds and finite action integrals. In a finite spectral frame, the counterterm is added to the covariant connection because the response one-form enters that connection with a minus sign. This line result determines more than the normalized state. It does not claim a convergent bare infinite determinant product or a global holonomy theorem.

    A cap is a chosen filling of a boundary together with fields, boundary conditions and normalization that prepare a vector or functional in the specified boundary state space. If an anomaly makes the amplitude line-valued, that line belongs to the data. For a bulk observable OO, an exact cap comparison would take the form

    ZMbulk(O)=ZM∂(rM(O)),Z_M^{\mathrm{bulk}}(O) =Z_M^{\partial}\bigl(r_M(O)\bigr),
    (17.9)

    where rMr_M is the actual observable comparison and both sides take values in an identified amplitude line. This equation is a target, not a definition of ZM∂Z_M^{\partial} by the left-hand side. The state prepared by the filling must be constructed independently, and the comparison must commute with cutting and gluing.

    The ordinary zero-height finite-stage Ward and full-source heat identities are defined pieces of this problem. They include all physical components on that domain and retain the complete first quantum transport W0+χW1W^0+\chi W^1, where χ=−ℏ\chi=-\hbar. They do not supply the missing uncut-to-cut comparison, the higher collision operations or the cap. Nor can the numerical state and the local line be combined outside a proved common source domain merely because both use the symbol μ\mu.

    17.6 Independent realizations test what reconstruction preserves

    The geometric and arithmetic families provide decisive tests of the same distinctions. In the M2 junction of Chapter 14, the group Tor1⁡\operatorname{Tor}_1, in cohomological degree −1-1, vanishes, but a flux cap from Tor2⁡\operatorname{Tor}_2, in cohomological degree −2-2, survives at every positive rank and nonzero numerical ℏ\hbar. Ordinary tensor composition gives the expected quotient, while the derived interface retains an additional bimodule. A reconstruction preserving only ordinary products would miss the flux operation.

    For compact states, Chapter 15 constructs relative Donaldson–Thomas operators before taking their traces. Their closure gives the inverse-Igusa series with its fixed normalization. The full three-boundary operation contains information that these traces omit: an explicit nonzero cyclic Hochschild class changes the state product while leaving the fibre-marked operation and every stated multiplication trace unchanged. Thus a numerical identity can be an exact theorem without characterizing the state algebra that produces it.

    Arithmetic gives a related example with a different meaning. The integer-summation and theta constructions retain the full multiplicities and produce the complete Weil trace. A positive representation of the critical part is also constructed. Its missing trace is exactly the contribution of nonreal centred zeros. The full positivity problem remains stronger than continuous duality or the existence of a cyclic vector. Integral normal operations further distinguish arithmetic tubes from their scalar points.

    These results explain what a common theory must preserve: actions as well as spaces, operations as well as counts, collision extensions as well as separated restrictions, and amplitude lines as well as normalized states. They also give actual constructions from which comparisons can start. The remaining questions are not requests to replace these theorems by a single slogan. They ask for the specific additional maps that let the constructions compose. The final chapter states those questions on their original domains.

    Part V Reconstruction and open problemsChapter 18 of 18

    18

    The strongest remaining questions

    The preceding constructions leave several exact comparison problems. Some ask for a map between independently defined objects; others ask whether a known map is an equivalence on a larger domain. A counterexample to one proposed extension can coexist with a theorem on another domain. The problem statements below retain that distinction, so that a successful construction has an unambiguous conclusion and a failed comparison has a precise meaning.

    The shared objective is to recover local operations, representations, states and amplitudes together. The questions are connected by that objective, but their coefficients and categories differ. A solution in one family transfers to another only through an actual comparison preserving the data named in the statement.

    18.1 The physical adjunction and its full domain

    Problem 18.1. Compare the functor defined by the prescribed physical boundary or interface with the tensor–Hom realization of the line algebra, including its right adjoint, unit and counit on the original complexes. Determine its essential image and its compatibility with the position-dependent product of line operators.

    The algebraic starting point is strong. At nonrational 𝔰𝔩3\mathfrak{sl}_3 parameter, the fourth derived tensor power of the positive ideal vanishes and its third power does not. Under the stated smooth realization data, the actual unit is invertible on every ordinary unbounded line module. Its image is the localizing category generated by the regular-top affine object and all required internal shifts. The corresponding nonrational 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 theorem has a two-step descent. Inflated coefficients have a unit theorem for every simple type and level under their realization hypotheses. Chapter 6

    The unresolved comparison is not supplied by those hypotheses themselves. One must identify the field-theoretic right adjoint with the constructed one, with its support, signs, action and higher naturality. For other simple types at nonrational parameter, a finite descent mechanism would need a theorem on the actual bimodule tensor powers or on the tensor powers of the fibre-inclusion map. Ordinary ideal nilpotence is insufficient.

    The native precision-three example gives a specific action test. Its all-input dg quantum vertex fields induce ordinary local cohomology fields at every numerical level. Yet, at noncritical level, the two marked evaluations have the same nonzero derived bimodule obstruction for the specified quotient-inflated source action. A source resolution cannot remove it. The next physical comparison must change the obstructed action or recipient and compare the replacement with the original operations. The field theorem and exact endpoint obstruction.

    There is now a comparison before this physical step. Retained kernels give continuous evaluations on the ordered rooted carrier at every numerical level. At K≠−2K\ne-2, a homotopy with zero scalar pairing aligns the prescribed and field-defined evaluations through middle degree one. Let Φ\Phi be the prescribed retained kernel, let 𝒴♯,1\mathcal Y^{\sharp,1} be its first-root-corrected field counterpart, and let 𝒞\mathscr C be the retained Hom subcomplex imposing homogeneity, both translation laws and zero scalar pairing. The higher retained question is

    [Φ−𝒴♯,1]=0in H0(𝒞).[\Phi-\mathcal Y^{\sharp,1}]=0 \quad\text{in }H^0(\mathscr C).

    Its displayed representative vanishes on inserted ghost degrees zero and one. A reduction to the two trace-free state generators must still extend over every trace-current polynomial and trace-ghost monomial with these constraints. Scalar normalization does not give strict creation-unit preservation, and the correction need not begin at order ℏ2\hbar^2. Even a solution of this higher retained problem must still be extended to the full marked and whole-series coefficient source, the proper unit cones and the independent physical operations. Retained kernels and the first rooted comparison.

    Raw 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 level −3-3 provides a discriminating case. Its weight-zero quotient kills a nonzero telescope whose affine realization survives; every finite fibre-inclusion power for that quotient is nonzero. This rules out finite descent through that quotient. It leaves open the full unit theorem and the different descent route through the ghost quotient. Critical and specified negative levels have genuine realization kernels, so a theorem covering all levels cannot retain the same ordinary source category without accounting for those kernels.

    The unbounded essential-image problem is equally precise. The cellular category, the full subcategory with torsion cohomology, and the derived category of the torsion abelian category are three different constructions. A proposed identification must survive the product-modulo-sum class of Chapter 6. Termwise torsion and bounded-below torsion cohomology already give positive cellularity theorems; those results do not remove the unbounded comparison.

    For algebraically energy-graded positive-current 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2, a common annihilating tail on all sufficiently low cohomology now makes the actual smooth-vector completion unit invertible. This does not prove generation by the shifted trivial modules: a nonzero torsion-null object could still be complete. The common-tail theorem and its generation boundary.

    18.2 General chiral quantum groups and completed curved duality

    Problem 18.2. For the independently defined chiral field and mode constructions, construct a compatible associative product, same-position tensor, coproduct and exchange on the required category of representations. Identify the relevant curved dual category and the exact localization in which its comparison functors are inverse.

    The spectral class already has explicit fields, a cross-contracted tensor product, level-indexed coproducts, their coassociativity and counit identities, and a field hexagon. The rational determinant-one matrix comparison holds in every rank N≥2N\ge2 and at every numerical level, with divided integral relations and ℏ\hbar-adic fields. Nonlinear quadratic–linear–scalar algebras have derivative-corrected curved transposes. The regular universal W3W_3 mode algebra has actual curved bar adjoints at every finite charge. Chapter 12

    The remaining module comparison must preserve the full mixed curvature, rather than only the regular half-ghost quotient. It must specify the summation monad, completed tensors and weak equivalences. A contramodule need not come with an underlying topology, and an ordinary state-field theorem does not decide those choices. For W3W_3, the known smooth objects and iterated-continuous derived Hom provide concrete tests for the proposed localization.

    Exceptional W4W_4 fibres give another finite test. Their complete dimension table and three primitive products are known, including η5η7=0\eta_5\eta_7=0. The products involving the extra classes, the positive torsion exponents and associative formality at those fibres remain to be determined. Replacing them by the generic exterior algebra would erase the observed jump. A construction of the full exceptional algebra must reproduce the known products before drawing a conclusion about formality.

    18.3 Universal actions and higher residue compatibility

    Problem 18.3. Decide whether multiplication and vacuum evaluation identify the full character and action spaces for every admitted pointed factorizing actor, and construct a comparison with the ordinary vertex-algebra mapping spaces wherever the two descriptions are claimed to agree.

    For the geometric spaces of Chapter 7, the maps are

    Θ(g)=m(g⊗!1),Ψ(α)=α(1⊗!uB).\Theta(g)=m(g\otimes^!1), \qquad \Psi(\alpha)=\alpha(1\otimes^!u_B).

    Their types, pointings and homotopy fibres are fixed. Recognition is established on the stated unital, module-extension and nonunital families. The original pointed three-block boundary is filled for arbitrary unbounded coassociative actors without a cocommutativity hypothesis. A different separated-base primitive comparison uses coherent cocommutativity of the underlying actor. The general question still requires all root changes, collision restrictions and arbitrarily long refinements.

    The ordinary binary exterior source has a separate complete theorem, including unbounded noncommutative targets. Its exact interpolation uses actual quotients and strict factorizations of transitions. To use that theorem in the geometric action problem, the comparison must retain both legs of roofs, evaluation and the full refinement diagrams. Identifying tangent complexes or singleton cohomology does not construct that map.

    The residue complexes supply a concrete higher-dimensional problem. For Dr,q(b,N;μ)D_{r,q}(b,N;\mu), the strict statement is

    Hn(Dr,q)=0(q≥2, n<q),H^n(D_{r,q})=0\qquad(q\ge2,\ n<q),
    (18.1)

    with positive odd μ\mu and the specified pole bounds. It holds for three spectators with arbitrary nonnegative bounds, for two spectators, and for arbitrary spectator count when the marked–spectator bounds vanish; further fixed positive-bound cases are known. The uniform first compatibility ideal is also computed. The second and later compatibility defects at arbitrary spectator count remain distinct questions. A fixed-bound class at n=qn=q prevents replacing the strict inequality by n≤qn\le q, while its possible death under enlarged pole bounds remains compatible with an eventual comparison. Chapter 7

    The genuine Heisenberg actor comparison has a more concrete remaining test. Let F0F^0 be the whole zero sector of its charge and constant detector, and let UU be the genuine pointed automorphism space of H⊕︎ϵHH\oplus\epsilon H acting trivially on state cohomology. The original qBq_B is an equivalence exactly when F0F^0 is connected and UU is contractible. Neither condition is settled; based loop calculations alone cannot see an additional zero-sector component. Genuine fibre reduction.

    18.4 Integral collisions and independently completed intermediate objects

    Problem 18.4. Construct the comparison between the integral collision objects, the common radial current construction and independently defined nested tensor products, preserving the original rational evaluations and all incoming and outgoing actions.

    Under the coherent realization, full-unit, bounded-below cellularity and two-term inflated-descent hypotheses stated in Chapter 8, its theorem covers every finite number of radial inputs on the declared F((q))F((q)) domain and original jointly nilpotent smooth tests. The complete incoming bar has its own perturbative contraction; the outgoing realization uses a separate algebraic bar. Finite integral heads have actual derived base-change and collision maps. These are different pieces of the comparison, not absent operations waiting to be defined from scratch.

    The obstruction is equally explicit: the radial field admits coefficient sequences for which substitution into a nested separation has no lower Laurent bound. A valid extension must prove a uniform support condition on its own space, or construct a different map that retains the same evaluations. Collision specialization must be performed before inverting the discriminant. An argument that substitutes a collision into the separated Laurent field has not reached the integral question.

    The full three-pole rational tensorator and native joint comparison hold for arbitrary constant ordinary inputs under the retained realization hypotheses. Reaching the independently factorized endpoint retains finite-total spectator cohomology. For arbitrary constant T=T12⊗M3T=T_{12}\otimes M_3, there is nevertheless an actual common domain LDfac=LD∩N1L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}=L_D\cap N_1: at each outer Laurent coefficient the spectator has finite algebraic support across the inner series. It maps to the radial object and the independently completed pair-first object. Finite total cohomology of M3M_3 makes its inclusion into LDL_D a quasi-isomorphism; the raw comparison cones remain, and the inflated regular UU-module still gives a nonzero joint/factorized defect. The defined carriers and common-domain theorem.

    Two independently completed pairs also have an algebraic comparison, with separate factorized, symmetric and ordered carriers. Finite total cohomology of both pairs gives equivalences after the specified extensions to either ordered field. The factorized conic intersection uses the smaller ring D∗=Dcon∩Λfac((q))D_*=D_{\mathrm{con}}\cap\Lambda_{\mathrm{fac}}((q)), defined by the conic and separated-cluster support conditions; it is generally not a module over all of DconD_{\mathrm{con}}. The full four-pole rational tensorator has its algebraic bar identities. A native full-bar interchange, its compatibility with associativity in larger trees and its original topology remain further constructions. Two independently completed clusters.

    The next current comparison must evaluate the full regular kernel on an incoming bar adapted to the factorized intersection, with support uniform in incoming bar length for each fixed outgoing word. It must also retain the original integral collision heads, a nonzero normal jet, the actual comparison cones and the native outer topology. Ordinary HomD⁡\operatorname{Hom}_D on arbitrary ring-defined tests fails quasi-isomorphism invariance; explicit finite WDW_D-cell models give a positive comparison without that false extension. The test-category distinction.

    Normalized-vacuum deletion is available in all three slots on full ambient field tests and constant ground-field tests for DD. The third slot retains its nonanchored output chart. Constant spectral inputs at any finite number of points have a flat chain connection, with outgoing horizontality up to specified homotopies. These gains leave the anchored test-coordinate comparison, integral deletion and opposite insertions, the normalized full-complex gauge with its inverse and action homotopies, and the current/native comparisons over polynomial parameter forms with all facets and interchanges. Deletion and the spectral connection.

    For mixed boundary currents, the required domain also includes real height gates and distributional contacts. The finite marked Ward calculus, radial circuit transport and normalized endpoint refinements are established with their stated support and regularity. A general height trace without a retained real normal is false; stronger spectator hypotheses give positive trace results. The next comparison must retain these different domains rather than erase them by calling every operation a distribution. Chapter 8 and Chapter 9

    Problem 18.5. Extend analytic conformal-block composition to the required unsmoothed source and target spaces, with both descent conditions and all composition maps retained.

    Under the normalized boundary hypothesis of Chapter 10—convergent algebraic four-point channel sewings, canonical spectral L2L^2 channel vectors, the prescribed real unitary fusion transformation and normalized positive-label pentagon—and its two-radius estimates, the available analytic theorem constructs finite uncut tree compositions and identity insertions on specified completions. Its obstructions distinguish a missing diagonal limit from failure of descent through a quotient. A proposed unrestricted sewing theorem must control the actual noncut domains, outgoing quotient and convergence of the original maps. Compatibility on a dense algebraic core is not sufficient without the continuity and closedness statements used in the extension. Chapter 10

    18.5 The compact elliptic attachment

    Problem 18.6. Identify the original compact output with the independently specified elliptic evaluation on the full supported contact image, preserving the cylinder comparison and all prescribed lower homotopies.

    The reduction in Chapter 9 isolates the actual remaining map:

    Aϵδu−Eϵδc=∂ℒϵ+γϵgrδc,γϵ=Aϵjqjr−Eϵjr.A_\epsilon\delta_u-E_\epsilon\delta_c =\partial\mathcal L_\epsilon +\gamma_\epsilon g_r\delta_c, \qquad \gamma_\epsilon=A_\epsilon j_qj_r-E_\epsilon j_r.
    (18.2)

    All terms have the original coefficient and support domains described there. Thus the task is to control γϵ\gamma_\epsilon on that image and to provide the cylinder map on the homotopy outputs where it is needed. A coordinate identification of finite normal spaces is not that cylinder map.

    The full Hom differential retains the antiholomorphic descendants of scalar rows. At cubic order, every term in

    Ω0P3+Ω1P2+Ω2P1+Ω3P0\Omega_0P_3+\Omega_1P_2+\Omega_2P_1+\Omega_3P_0

    survives unless an actual identity removes it. Adjusting lower homotopies contributes −∂1S2−∂2S1−∂3S0-\partial_1S_2-\partial_2S_1-\partial_3S_0. The finite polynomial boundary limits, supported compositions and vanishing scalar comparison values remain useful theorems. They do not determine these remaining maps after a scalar trace has discarded their outputs.

    18.6 The gravitational state, line and cap

    Problem 18.7. Compare the numerical bulk state, the original based vacuum line and the state prepared by the prescribed geometric filling, on a common field and source domain and with cutting and gluing preserved.

    The normalized numerical Gaussian and its full graded Wick moments are constructed on the original continued cycles. The coefficient heat has a finite part and a based local line section, with the correct covariant source counterterm. The ordinary zero-height finite-stage Ward identity and first quantum heat cells retain the complete first transport term. None of these results needs to be replaced by a formal covariance chosen after the integral. Chapter 11

    On the square-zero reflected Ward family, a common gapped positive-level interval and the fixed-scale uniform inserted heat expansion give the relative formula Wfp(x1)−Wfp(x0)=∫x0x1cF(x)dx/xW_{\mathrm{fp}}(x_1)-W_{\mathrm{fp}}(x_0)=\int_{x_0}^{x_1}c_F(x)\,dx/x. The absolute Mellin comparison retains γEC\gamma_E C. This positive-interval theorem supplies neither a zero-level endpoint estimate nor an independent geometric cap. On a sufficiently small common based family the local line and normalized numerical state do form a continuous line-valued functional; identifying it with the cap remains the stated problem. Positive-level variation and its endpoint.

    The missing cap comparison must supply the map from uncut coefficient fields to the fields on the geometric cut, identify the amplitude lines and transport the normalized observable functionals together with the base amplitude. A global line statement must determine holonomy and anomaly data beyond one local source neighbourhood. An interacting boundary theorem must extend the insertion identities to its actual normal derivatives, positive-height roots, singular higher collisions and quantum orders. The existing ordinary unary result does not assert those extensions.

    One precise issue is the relation between formal perturbation and the numerical cycle limit. At a finite spectral window, the covariance correction and determinant-line ratio give an actual formal comparison. An infinite-dimensional conclusion needs convergence of the original series in the same topology and identification of its sum with the numerical state. Equality of finite formal coefficients alone does not establish that analytic statement.

    18.7 Brane junctions and geometric state operations

    Problem 18.8. Construct the open–closed map from the independently specified bulk fields to the derived operations on branes and interfaces, preserving both outer actions, junction composition and the flux class.

    For the M2 particle junction, the degree-two cap onto ANA_N is a split bimodule surjection at every positive rank and nonzero numerical ℏ\hbar. Its kernel multiplicities for N≥2N\ge2 and the higher algebra structure on the full derived tensor product remain unknown. The cap does not make the derived multiplication an equivalence. The integral curved matrix comparison and polynomial Hamiltonian transport supply different positive constructions on their declared rank and degree ranges. The physical comparison must carry the actual fields into these objects. Chapter 14

    For the D3 sector, the exact chiral image and simplicity are known, together with specific higher torsion and nonseparated phenomena. A comparison to an independently defined Kodaira–Spencer bulk must preserve that derived information. For surface fusion, the rank-addition Miura map is algebraically coassociative, but its identification with the five-dimensional fusion operation needs the quantized defect, Ward identities and normalization. Higher-current and celestial constructions likewise have explicit finite or special nonabelian scopes; their extension must retain the central and anomaly terms present there.

    Problem 18.9. Compare the critical Hall coefficient theory with the full compact state theory before taking traces, preserving orientation roots, relative moment values, the ordinary unit, pairing and reduced three-boundary operation.

    The ordinary K3 composition Hall comparison is faithful, strong orientation exists on the stated two-charge component group, and the spherical reduced coefficient maps are constructed in every positive length. Relative Donaldson–Thomas operators, untraced multiple covers and the primitive inverse-Igusa trace are also established. The global flag comparison must still retain its common lifting gerbes and relative moment parameters; imposing separate zero moments on every intermediate object would change it.

    The state-map target is H∗(S[d])H^*(S^{[d]}) with its actual pairing and products. At d=1d=1, the trace-invisible cyclic deformation of Chapter 15 changes a nonzero three-state coefficient while keeping the stated trace data. A realization must distinguish those products and preserve the geometric one. Equivariant orientation descent and comparison with independently chosen compact orientations are further specified arrows, not consequences of an orientation sign on numerical charges. Chapter 15

    18.8 Arithmetic positivity and local operations

    Problem 18.10. Establish

    W(g∗g∗)≥0for every g∈Cc∞(ℝ;ℂ),W(g*g^*)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb C),

    or construct an independently defined ordinary positive representation whose trace is the complete Weil functional on its stated test algebra.

    The exact missing contribution in the existing positive representation is

    W(f)−Tr⁡πcrit(f)=∑wρ∉ℝmρfˆ(wρ).W(f)-\operatorname{Tr}\pi_{\mathrm{crit}}(f) =\sum_{w_\rho\notin\mathbb R}m_\rho\widehat f(w_\rho).
    (18.3)

    Its vanishing on all tests has Riemann-hypothesis strength. The fixed whole-window theorem already proves positivity for every complex L2L^2 test supported in an interval of width at most 31/1031/10, with both parity certificates and full coupling bounds. A theorem on larger cofinal windows must retain the prime-power, polar, real-place and off-block terms. For a block decomposition, the relevant form is the Schur complement A−K∗D−1KA-K^*D^{-1}K; positivity of AA alone is not its required lower bound. Chapter 16

    Problem 18.11. Compare the independently defined arithmetic coefficient complexes with a local field theory and a common integrable trace domain, preserving multiplicity jets, normal operations, Frobenius variance, collisions and the vacuum.

    Continuous integer-summation duality, the full theta trace, actual completed bar homotopies and injective integral normal comparisons are available. The linking construction gives a cyclic vector and nonlocal creation fields; it does not give locality. At an arithmetic point, the relation h0h_0 vanishes on scalar evaluation but its first normal derivative is −p-p, nonzero modulo p2p^2. A local comparison factoring only through scalar points would destroy that operation. A full cyclic trace on the position–normal algebra is also constrained by [D0,Mx0]=pI[D_0,M_{x_0}]=pI, whereas proper trace ideals and specified finite residue functionals remain valid.

    These problems return to the original reduction question in a sharper form. The theory has explicit objects, maps, finite filtrations, state operations and counterexamples. A reconstruction theorem must carry their operations through the proposed comparison and show exactly where it is invertible. The next decisive result is therefore an equality, equivalence or obstruction for one of the specified maps, on the domain where that map has a mathematical meaning.

    Research programme

    Quantum holography and associative chiral Koszul duality

    Fields, dualities, fusion, bulk observables and quantum states across the programme.

    Last updated 16 November 2026, 16:20 UTC · Contents

    The programme relates field algebras, configuration operations, module categories, bulk observables and quantum states through maps that preserve singular composition. Ordered configurations retain where insertions meet, which input comes first and how cuts and collisions interact.

    Complete bar–cobar and mode-duality theorems now sit beside recognition for every pointing on the stated actors, the full ordinary binary Centre comparison, current comparisons for arbitrary unbounded binary inputs and normalized numerical Gaussian states. Their exact morphisms, units and source domains determine which constructions compose.

    The remaining work includes genuine roof-to-action maps, unsmoothed composite analytic operations, physical state and cutoff comparisons, global arithmetic positivity and untraced geometric products. Scoped counterexamples retain their specified data; they do not erase positive constructions on other domains.

    The twenty families and twenty-two decisive questions keep the whole programme in view, from currents and quantum fields to Hall geometry, branes, gravity and arithmetic. The current account distinguishes the theorem already achieved from the stronger map still to be constructed.
